title: pre-commit hook blocks commits on pre-existing PHPCS warnings
body:
## Problem

`.githooks/pre-commit` runs `vendor/bin/phpcs --colors "$FILE"` and treats any non-zero exit as failure. PHPCS exits 1 when a file has **warnings only**. Any edit to a file with pre-existing warnings is therefore blocked, even when the change adds no errors.

Example: `inc/models/class-base-model.php` has 6 pre-existing warnings (`PSR2.Classes.PropertyDeclaration.Underscore` on `$_original`, `$_mappings`, `$_mocked`; `Squiz.PHP.CommentedOutCode.Found` at about lines 732/737; `PSR2.Methods.MethodDeclaration.Underscore` on `_get_original`) and 0 errors. Committing #2004 failed with "Could not fully fix", and PHPCBF reported "No fixable errors were found".

## Fix

- File: `.githooks/pre-commit` (the `phpcs` calls at about lines 42, 60 and 75).
- Make the pass/fail checks ignore warnings, e.g. `vendor/bin/phpcs -n` or `--runtime-set ignore_warnings_on_exit 1`. Still show warnings for information if needed.

## Verification

- Stage a whitespace-only change to `inc/models/class-base-model.php` and run `git commit`. The hook passes, and PHPStan still runs.
- Stage a real PHPCS error (e.g. a non-Yoda comparison in `inc/`). The hook still blocks the commit.

### Files Scope

- `.githooks/pre-commit`

title: Secondary networks never get Ultimate Multisite tables created or upgraded
body:
## Problem

Ultimate Multisite only creates and upgrades its tables on the **main network**. On any other network in the same database it queries `wp_wu_{N}_*` tables but never creates them, and existing secondary-network tables never receive schema upgrades.

- `inc/database/engine/class-table.php`: `is_upgradeable()` returns false unless `is_main_network()`. BerlinDB's `maybe_upgrade()` (on `admin_init`) is the only automatic install/upgrade path, so it never runs on other networks. This has been the case since the initial commit.
- The only other path is `Core_Installer::_install_database_tables()` (setup wizard), which calls `$table->install()` directly.
- Multinetwork's cloner only creates unsuffixed `wp_wu_*` tables in tenant databases. Nothing creates `wp_wu_{N}_*` for networks in the same database.
- Tables with `$upgrades` (9 classes, e.g. `2.13.2`, `2.17.4`) are never upgraded on secondary networks.

### Reproduction

On current `main`, create network 3 (`wu_create_network()`) and mark setup finished. `Table_Loader` registers `wp_wu_3_customers`, but `is_upgradeable()` is false and `exists()` is false, and `wu_get_customers()` fails with `Table '…wu_3_customers' doesn't exist`.

## Fix

1. `Engine\Table::is_upgradeable()`: allow the main site of any network (`is_main_site()`).
2. On secondary networks, run each table's `maybe_upgrade()` on the first request (front end included), gated by one per-network option holding the tables' schema signature, so it runs once per schema change. Per-network version keys already exist (`wpdb_wu_{N}_{table}_version`, stored on the main network).

### Files

- `inc/database/engine/class-table.php`
- `inc/loaders/class-table-loader.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Database/Engine/Table_Test.php`

## Verification

- A new secondary network gets all plugin tables on its first request, and model queries have no DB errors.
- A secondary-network table with an older recorded version runs its pending upgrade.
- The main network behaves as before. Later requests don't re-run the check (a single option read).

title: Secondary networks: sunrise queries unregistered scoped tables, and wu_{N}_* tables are never created
body:
## Problem

On a multi-network install, Ultimate Multisite queries network-scoped tables (`{base_prefix}wu_{network_id}_*`) on secondary networks, but two paths leave those tables unusable:

1. **Sunrise domain mapping queries tables that were never registered.** `Sunrise::load_domain_mapping()` (`inc/class-sunrise.php:191-205`) starts `Domain_Mapping` on every network. On a network where Ultimate Multisite returns before `setup_tables()` (`inc/class-wp-ultimo.php`, the `Requirements::met() === false || Requirements::run_setup() === false` early return; `run_setup()` reads the per-network `wu_setup_finished` option), no `Table` object is built for that network. The domain `Query` still applies the network prefix (`Network_Prefix::update_prefix_with_network_id()`, `inc/database/engine/traits/trait-network-prefix.php:20-25`), so it reads `$wpdb->wu_{N}_domain_mappings`. That property is unset, which gives an empty table name:

   ```
   Table '<db>.wu_5_d' doesn't exist for query SELECT  wu_5_d.id FROM  wu_5_d WHERE wu_5_d.blog_id = 323 AND wu_5_d.domain != ...
   ```

   Note the double space: the table name is empty and only the alias `wu_5_d` remains. Production logged about 170 of these in 7 hours on one template network.

2. **Secondary-network tables are never created.** `Table::is_upgradeable()` (`inc/database/engine/class-table.php:50-57`) returns false unless the request is on the main network and main site, so `maybe_upgrade()` never installs `wp_wu_{N}_*`. A network ends up with none of these tables, or with only the subset some one-off path created. One network had customers/memberships/payments but no `posts`, `postmeta`, `webhooks`, `passkey_credentials`, `webauthn_challenges`, `email_otp_attempts` or `sso_nonces`. Addon tables that extend the core `Table` (e.g. metered-plans' `metered_usage`) inherit the same gap. A missing `posts` table also means a network has no system emails (`payment_received_*`, `site_published_*`, …).

## Expected

- Every secondary network that Ultimate Multisite serves has its full set of scoped tables, created idempotently when the network is first used or created, and on upgrade.
- Domain mapping at sunrise never builds a query against an unregistered table. Either register the network's tables (e.g. build the needed `Table` objects in `Sunrise::load_domain_mapping()` before `Domain_Mapping` runs), or fall back to the main network's tables when Ultimate Multisite is not set up on the current network.
- Default system emails get created for a network once its `posts` table exists.

## Workaround applied on one install (not a fix)

Ran in each affected network's `--url` context:
- `$t->install()` for every `Table_Loader::get_instance()->get_tables()` entry, plus `Metered_Usage_Table`, where `exists()` was false.
- `Email_Manager::get_instance()->create_all_system_emails()`.
- For the template network, set the `wu_setup_finished` network option so Ultimate Multisite completes loading and registers its tables.

Note: `Table::exists()` caches its result, so in the same process it still reported false right after a successful `install()`. A fresh process or `information_schema` showed the tables were present.

## Files to modify

- `inc/class-sunrise.php` (`load_domain_mapping`)
- `inc/database/engine/class-table.php` (`is_upgradeable`, and possibly the `exists()` cache)
- `inc/installers/class-core-installer.php` (network-scoped install)
- `inc/loaders/class-table-loader.php`
- `inc/managers/class-email-manager.php` (`create_all_system_emails` on new networks)

## Verification

On a multi-network test install:
1. Create a secondary network without running the setup wizard and request one of its mapped domains. There should be no `FROM  wu_N_` (empty table) errors.
2. Every `get_tables()` entry should `exists()` for that network after creation or upgrade.
3. `wu_get_emails()` should return the default system emails on that network.


### Files Scope

- `inc/class-sunrise.php`
- `inc/database/engine/class-table.php`
- `inc/installers/class-core-installer.php`
- `inc/loaders/class-table-loader.php`
- `inc/managers/class-email-manager.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Database/Engine/Table_Test.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Managers/Email_Manager_Test.php`

title: perf: lazy-load the top My Sites toolbar and defer initial site-list hydration
body:
## What

Lazy-load the **top WordPress My Sites toolbar dropdown beside My Networks** so an unopened menu does not enumerate and hydrate the full site list or construct every site's management links. This is not the bottom-right Toolbox/Jumper UI.

Keep current-site navigation and an explicit full My Sites administration link immediately available. Fetch bounded, paginated results only when the menu is opened or explicitly requested, preserving the existing site visibility rules, permissions and SSO/magic links.

## Why / measured evidence

Read-only authenticated local Users-request profiling, with the My Networks lazy-loading change already served:

| Region | Typical local elapsed | SQL queries | Blog-context events |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Initial Ultimate Multisite site-list preparation | 0.166–0.204s | 113 | 58 |
| WordPress My Sites submenu construction | 0.120–0.130s | 22 | 60 |
| Combined initial preparation plus menu | 0.2867s median across 3 runs | 135 | 118 |

Events count both switches and restores, not 118 distinct sites. Later site-list calls were already largely request-cached and added no SQL. The bottom Toolbox setup/render cost about 4ms and no additional SQL on the same request; do not optimize that unrelated UI for this issue.

These are inclusive instrumented CLI request-attribution measurements, not production HTTP savings. One additional run was substantially slower with identical operation counts, so do not promise a fixed latency reduction. Persistent Redis was disabled locally. Verify with controlled HTTP runs after implementing.

## Root cause and verified files

- `inc/managers/class-site-manager.php:1158-1277`, `hide_customer_sites_from_super_admin_list()`: builds up to 40 site objects plus the main site. Reads of `$site->blogname` and `$site->siteurl` hydrate WordPress site details and activate downstream blog-switch hooks.
- `inc/managers/class-site-manager.php:1280-1362`, `is_frontend_my_sites_toolbar_request()` and `get_current_site_for_frontend_my_sites_toolbar()`: existing **opt-in, frontend-only, direct-toolbar-initialization** optimization is a reference pattern. It intentionally excludes admin/AJAX/REST/CLI and protects nested `get_active_blog_for_user()` calls. Do not simply remove those guards.
- `inc/sso/class-admin-bar-magic-links.php`: existing My Sites node rewriting must remain effective for lazily loaded links.
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Managers/Site_Manager_Test.php`: existing toolbar context, filtering, user scope and archived/spam/deleted tests.
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/SSO/Admin_Bar_Magic_Links_Test.php`: existing magic-link coverage.
- `DESIGN.md`: record the changed interaction and fallback behavior.

Reference the WordPress core `WP_Admin_Bar::initialize()` / `get_blogs_of_user()` preparation path and `wp_admin_bar_my_sites_menu()` separately. Deferring just the submenu callback leaves the initial 113-query hydration cost intact. Core lives in the WordPress installation, not in this plugin repository; inspect its installed implementation rather than guessing repository paths.

Use the existing site manager for the authenticated endpoint and add `assets/js/my-sites-toolbar.js` for the native toolbar controller, following existing asset conventions. If investigation requires a different write surface, record and validate the amended scope before editing. Related implementation reference: Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-multinetwork#63, which lazy-loads My Networks with pagination, nonce checks, retry and keyboard/touch support. It is a reference, not an implementation dependency or an assumption that the PR has merged.

### Files Scope

- `inc/managers/class-site-manager.php`
- `inc/sso/class-admin-bar-magic-links.php`
- NEW: `assets/js/my-sites-toolbar.js`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Managers/Site_Manager_Test.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/SSO/Admin_Bar_Magic_Links_Test.php`
- `DESIGN.md`

## Bounded implementation contract

1. Restrict the lightweight initial site-list behavior to the direct toolbar initialization context; do not globally change `get_blogs_of_user()` for profile links, dashboards, admin screens, REST clients or application code.
2. Preserve existing allowed-site filtering and current-user context. The lazy endpoint must be authenticated, nonce-protected and server-authorized. Do not expose unrelated sites, globally cache capability decisions, or weaken authorization.
3. Return at most 10–20 sites per fetch, with deterministic ordering and explicit pagination. Do not preload the complete list in script localization or hidden HTML.
4. Preserve network/site-specific URLs, customer-owned-site visibility semantics, existing `get_blogs_of_user` filters and magic-link/SSO behavior. Restore any switched context in a `finally` block.
5. Retain current-site and full-list navigation without JavaScript. Support hover, keyboard focus and touch; provide loading, empty and explicit retry states, no duplicate in-flight requests, and no focus theft on hover.
6. Cover admin and frontend toolbar paths. Do not modify WordPress core or unrelated installed plugins. Do not enable the existing frontend optimization setting globally as a substitute for this implementation.

## Acceptance / verification

- [ ] Unopened toolbar does not perform full managed-site enumeration/detail hydration or per-site submenu construction.
- [ ] Opening the menu fetches only a bounded page; load-more results are disjoint and full-list access remains available.
- [ ] Verify current-site navigation and generated links under both subdomain and subdirectory multisite, mapped domains and secondary networks where available.
- [ ] Preserve permission denial, customer/non-super-admin behavior, site-state filtering and magic-link behavior. No cross-user/site information disclosure.
- [ ] Keyboard activation, Escape/focus return, touch layout, failed-request retry and JavaScript-disabled fallback work in the real rendered product.
- [ ] Existing affected Site_Manager and Admin_Bar_Magic_Links suites pass, with only narrow new boundary coverage; no new test runner/harness is needed.
- [ ] Run scoped PHPCS/ESLint/PHPStan and inspect standard PHP/browser errors.
- [ ] Repeat authenticated HTTP before/after benchmarks with identical user pagination, revisions and cache configuration. Record actual HTTP time separately from CLI attribution; count both scalar and bulk cache-key reads and actual backend calls separately.
- [ ] Do not claim the 0.5-second target is reached without runtime evidence. Do not merge or deploy as part of worker implementation without the normal authorized lifecycle.

Rollback: revert the isolated lazy-toolbar change to restore the existing eager menu; no persistent data migration is required.

## Pre-flight and routing

- [x] Memory recall: My Sites toolbar/cache performance query returned no relevant stored lessons; current-session runtime evidence is supplied above.
- [x] Discovery: scoped recent-commit, merged-PR, open-PR and claimed-issue searches returned no matching work. Additional open searches for My Sites performance/toolbar returned no matches.
- [x] File references: the five implementation/test/design paths above were verified as tracked; line numbers reflect the inspected revision and must be rechecked at worker pickup.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — existing authorization patterns within a defined toolbar-only boundary; not a mechanical exact-edit task.
- [x] Seeded draft PR: skipped; preserve the measured finding without anchoring a worker to an unverified patch.

Leaf implementation task. Dispatch: #auto-dispatch. Create a focused implementation PR referencing this issue; no release or deployment is requested.

title: fix(sites): grid bulk Delete removes real sites matching pending sites' membership IDs
body:
## Bug: bulk "Delete" in the Sites grid view deletes real sites whose blog ID equals a pending site's membership ID

**Severity:** critical, silent data loss (site tables and uploads are dropped).

### What happens

In **Network Admin → Ultimate Multisite → Sites**, the default **grid view** of the "All Sites" tab renders pending sites with a selection checkbox whose value is the **membership ID**:

- `views/base/sites/grid-item.php` (pending branch): `name="bulk-delete[]" value="<?php echo esc_attr($item->get_membership_id()); ?>"`

The bulk action submitted from that tab is the regular `delete` action for model `site` (`Site_List_Table::get_bulk_actions()` only switches to `delete-pending` when `type=pending`). `Base_List_Table::process_bulk_action()` then runs `wu_get_site($id)->delete()` for every submitted ID, so each membership ID is treated as a **blog ID** and `wp_delete_site()` removes an unrelated live site.

The list view already guards against this (`Site_List_Table::column_cb()` omits pending checkboxes outside the dedicated Pending view), but the grid template does not.

### Reproduction

1. Have a pending site owned by membership `N`, and an unrelated published site with blog ID `N`.
2. Open Sites (grid view, All Sites), tick "Select Site" on the pending card, choose bulk **Delete**, confirm.
3. Blog `N` is deleted; the pending site remains.

Observed in production: selecting leftover pending test signups deleted three unrelated customer sites whose blog IDs matched the pending sites' membership IDs.

### Fix

- `views/base/sites/grid-item.php`: mirror `column_cb()` and render the pending checkbox only in the dedicated Pending view (`type=pending`), where the bulk action is `delete-pending` and membership IDs are the expected values.
- Defence in depth in `Base_List_Table::process_bulk_action()` / site bulk delete: refuse to delete when the request comes from a view that lists pending items with membership-ID values (or validate that submitted IDs are real blog IDs shown in that view).

### Verification

- Grid view, All Sites: pending cards show no bulk checkbox; bulk Delete of regular sites still works.
- Pending view: bulk delete removes only the pending-site records (`delete-pending`), no `wp_blogs` rows change.
- `vendor/bin/phpunit` for the site list / pending-site deletion tests; `vendor/bin/phpcs` on changed files.

title: Secondary networks: existing tables without a main-network version are stamped current without running upgrades
body:
## Problem

After #2013, a secondary network's first request runs `Table::maybe_install_network_table()` (`inc/database/engine/class-table.php`). For an **existing** `wu_{N}_*` table whose BerlinDB version key is missing, BerlinDB stamps the table as current **without running its upgrade callbacks**:

- `needs_upgrade()` reads `get_network_option(get_main_network_id(), "wpdb_wu_{N}_{table}_version")` (`vendor/berlindb/core/src/Database/Table.php:910-913`). Missing → `false` → upgrade needed.
- The table exists, so `upgrade()` runs. `get_pending_upgrades()` returns `[]` when `db_version` is empty (`Table.php:718`), so `upgrade()` calls `set_db_version()` with the current version and returns (`Table.php:679-684`).
- Then the table is recorded in `wu_network_table_versions` and never checked again until its version changes.

Two real-world states reach this path:

1. **Versions recorded under the secondary network's own `sitemeta`** (`site_id = N`) instead of the main network. Observed on a production install: one network had 38 `wpdb_wu_{N}_*_version` keys only under its own `site_id`, none under the main network. Another had 13 keys under both. Whatever wrote them (likely an install or upgrade run with `get_main_network_id()` resolving to the secondary network, e.g. the multinetwork add-on or a one-off installer) is not identified yet.
2. **Tables with no version key anywhere.** Observed: 4 tables on one secondary network (`forms`, `formmeta`, and two support-ticket add-on tables).

**Current impact: none observed.** Every recorded version on that install equals the current code version, and the one version-less core table with an upgrade callback (`wu_{N}_forms`) already has the post-`2.0.1-revision.20230601` schema (nullable `date_created`/`date_modified`). The risk is latent: a schema bump that ships before these networks are stamped, or an older network with pre-upgrade tables, would skip upgrades silently.

## Proposed fix

In `Table::maybe_install_network_table()`, before calling `upgrade()` on an existing table with no main-network version:

1. **Adopt a network-local version.** If `get_network_option($network_id, $this->db_version_key)` has a value, copy it to the main network key (BerlinDB's source of truth) so `get_pending_upgrades()` runs the right callbacks. Optionally delete the stray network-local key after the upgrade succeeds.
2. **No version anywhere.** Decide between:
   - (a) treat it as the oldest baseline and run all upgrade callbacks (current core callbacks are idempotent `ALTER ... MODIFY COLUMN`, but add-on callbacks such as metered-plans `add_cost_value_column` must be checked for idempotency), or
   - (b) keep BerlinDB's stamp-current behaviour, but log it (`wu_log_add`) so the drift is visible.

   Recommendation: (1) plus (2b) unless all registered callbacks are verified idempotent.

## Files

- `inc/database/engine/class-table.php`: `maybe_install_network_table()`.
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Database/Engine/Table_Test.php`: follow the pattern of `test_secondary_network_table_is_upgraded_on_first_request`, but record the old version under `site_id = N` instead of the main network and assert that the upgrade ran.
- Unknown: the code path that wrote versions under the secondary network's `site_id`. Search `set_db_version`, `get_main_network_id` filters, and the multinetwork add-on's installer to identify it.

## Verification

- A secondary table whose old version exists only under its own network's `sitemeta` runs its pending upgrade callbacks on first request (column nullability changes, as in the existing upgrade test).
- A version-less existing table is handled per the chosen option (upgrades run, or a log entry is written).
- The main network and already-stamped secondary networks are unchanged (one cached option read).

Ref #2013, Ref #2012

## Summary

Follow-up to #1925/#2030 (Phase 0 of the invoice font plan). Invoices containing Hebrew, Thai, Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Armenian or Georgian text currently fail with a raw `MpdfException: Cannot find TTF TrueType font file "..."`. `scripts/remove-mpdf-fonts.php` deletes the fonts mPDF's script-to-language mapping selects for those scripts. #2035 contains the failure, but the message is opaque to site owners.

Probe results (mPDF 8.3.1, plugin config `+aCJK`, `autoScriptToLang`, `autoLangToFont`):

| Script | Today | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Persian, Vietnamese | renders | covered by DejaVu Sans Condensed |
| Armenian, Georgian | throws | mPDF asks for `DejaVuSans.ttf`, deleted by the strip script |
| Hebrew, Thai, Hindi, Bengali, Tamil | throws | `TaameyDavidCLM-Medium.ttf`, `Garuda.ttf`, `FreeSerif.ttf` deleted |

A manual probe showed that remapping `dejavusans` to the retained `DejaVuSansCondensed*.ttf` renders Armenian and Georgian with no new font bytes.

## Scope

1. Remap `dejavusans` (and `dejavuserif` to the retained `DejaVuSerifCondensed*.ttf`) in `Invoice::get_missing_fontdata()`, following the existing `dejavusansmono` pattern.
2. Before `WriteHTML()`, check the rendered invoice text for scripts whose mPDF-selected font file is not on disk. Use mPDF's own `Ucdn::get_script()`, `ScriptToLanguage` and `LanguageToFont` so the check follows mPDF's real font choice and needs no hand-kept script list. If a font is missing, throw `WP_Ultimo\Exception\Runtime_Exception` naming the scripts, before mPDF fails midway.
3. Surface the error. The existing `wu_log_add(..., LogLevel::ERROR)` calls in `Email_Manager::attach_invoice_pdf()` and `Payment_Manager::invoice_viewer()` already feed `Logger::maybe_store_recent_error()`, which raises the network-admin notice. The message must be clear and under 300 characters. Network admins also see the specific message in the invoice viewer; customers keep the generic one.

Out of scope: adding font files, on-demand or downloadable font packs, and CJK (mPDF uses non-embedded Adobe CJK fonts there, which is a separate issue). Fonts stay packaged in the plugin.

## Files

- `inc/invoices/class-invoice.php`
- `inc/managers/class-payment-manager.php`
- `inc/managers/class-email-manager.php` (only if the log wording needs adjusting)
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Invoices/Invoice_Test.php`

Reference pattern: `Invoice::get_missing_fontdata()` and `Invoice::get_loggable_error()`.

## Verification

- `Invoice_Test`: Armenian and Georgian generate a PDF, Hebrew throws `Runtime_Exception` naming "Hebrew", and Latin and Arabic still pass.
- `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter 'Invoice_Test|Email_Manager_Test|Payment_Manager_Test'`

title: feat: package fonts for more invoice PDF languages (Hebrew, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar, Sinhala, Kannada, Telugu, Sindhi)
body:
## Summary

Package fonts so invoice PDFs render Hebrew, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar, Sinhala, Kannada, Telugu and Sindhi. Fonts stay packaged in the plugin. There are no on-demand downloads in this issue.

Follow-up to #1925, #2030 (PR #2035) and #2037 (PR #2038). #2038 added a pre-render check, `Invoice::get_unsupported_scripts()`. It uses mPDF's own script database and font mapping, and fails early with a clear, admin-visible error when the font mPDF would select for a script is not on disk. Once a font file is retained, that script passes the check with no code change. So this issue is mainly about **which mPDF font files to stop stripping**.

## Background (verified against mPDF 8.3.1)

`scripts/remove-mpdf-fonts.php` deletes mPDF's non-Latin fonts. It runs from the composer `post-install-cmd` and `post-update-cmd` hooks. Every build path goes through it: `package.json` `prebuild` (`composer install -o --no-dev`), `release.yml`, CI and `bin/deploy.sh`. Editing its `$fonts` list is the single control point.

The original mPDF package, as cached by composer, gives exact sizes. Today the plugin ships about 2.9 MB of fonts (DejaVu Sans/Serif Condensed regular and bold, FreeMono, Eeyek).

## Scope: fonts to retain (from mPDF's own bundle, about 1.76 MB uncompressed in total)

| Script | mPDF font name | Files to keep | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hebrew | `taameydavidclm` | `TaameyDavidCLM-Medium.ttf`, `TaameyDavidCLM-LICENSE.txt` | 96 KB |
| Thai | `garuda` | `Garuda.ttf`, `Garuda-Bold.ttf` | 113 KB |
| Lao | `dhyana` | `Dhyana-Regular.ttf`, `Dhyana-Bold.ttf`, `DhyanaOFL.txt` | 134 KB |
| Khmer | `khmeros` | `KhmerOS.ttf`, `KhmerOFL.txt` | 266 KB |
| Myanmar (and Tai Le) | `tharlon` | `Tharlon-Regular.ttf`, `TharlonOFL.txt` | 353 KB |
| Sinhala | `kaputaunicode` | `kaputaunicode.ttf` | 160 KB |
| Kannada | `lohitkannada` | `Lohit-Kannada.ttf`, `LohitKannadaOFL.txt` | 198 KB |
| Telugu | `pothana2000` | `Pothana2000.ttf` | 194 KB |
| Sindhi | `lateef` | `LateefRegOT.ttf`, `Lateef font OFL.txt` | 246 KB |

Notes:
- mPDF's `fontdata` for most of these defines only the regular style. Garuda has regular, bold, oblique and bold-oblique, and Dhyana has regular and bold. The invoice template uses `<strong>` (company name, headings), so bold and italic markup must not throw `Font "..." is not supported`. For each retained family, check which of `R/B/I/BI` mPDF's `fontdata` defines. Where a style is missing, or its file is not retained, add a remap in `Invoice::get_missing_fontdata()` to a retained file. Use the existing `dejavusansmono`, `dejavusans` and `dejavuserif` entries as the pattern. Do not retain Garuda's two oblique files (57 KB each); remap `I` and `BI` to `R` and `B`.
- Keep the licence texts listed above next to the fonts they cover. Before retaining each font, confirm it may be redistributed. mPDF already distributes these files, but Garuda, `kaputaunicode` and `Pothana2000` ship without a licence text in `ttfonts/`. If redistribution terms are unclear for any font, leave it stripped and say so in the PR.

## Files

- `scripts/remove-mpdf-fonts.php`: remove the listed font and licence file names from `$fonts`. Add a comment pointing to this issue. Keep a note that retained fonts must keep all four `fontdata` styles resolvable.
- `inc/invoices/class-invoice.php`: remaps in `get_missing_fontdata()` for missing styles only.
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Invoices/Invoice_Test.php`: extend the existing tests. #2038 added `test_get_unsupported_scripts` and `test_pdf_with_unsupported_script_throws_clear_error`. Hebrew and Thai are in those tests as examples of unsupported scripts, so move them to a "supported" assertion and pick a still-unsupported script (for example Devanagari) for the failure case.

Reference patterns: `Invoice::get_missing_fontdata()` and `Invoice::get_unsupported_scripts()`.

## Out of scope (separate decisions, not part of this issue)

- **Devanagari, Bengali, Gujarati, Gurmukhi, Tamil, Malayalam, Oriya, Thaana:** mPDF selects `freeserif`, which is 3.3 MB regular plus 1.3 MB bold (about 4.6 MB for regular and bold). This needs a size decision, or a spike on smaller per-script fonts. Noto per-script fonts are a candidate but have not been tested with mPDF's OpenType shaper.
- **CJK:** with `+aCJK`, mPDF uses non-embedded Adobe CJK fonts, so most viewers and phones show blanks. Embedded fonts are large (`Sun-ExtA` is 23 MB, `UnBatang` is 6.9 MB). This is its own decision.
- **Tibetan** (`jomolhari`, 2.3 MB), **Syriac** (OTF file), **Ethiopic** (619 KB) and historical scripts.
- On-demand or downloadable font packs.

## Verification

- For each script in the table, generate a PDF through the real `WP_Ultimo\Invoices\Invoice` class with sample text in the company name (bold via `<strong>`) and in a line item title. Render it with `pdftoppm` and inspect the image for correct glyph shaping, joining and ordering. A PDF header alone is not evidence. Suggested samples are in the #2037 PR body and `Invoice_Test`.
- `Invoice::get_unsupported_scripts()` returns `[]` for each of these scripts.
- Bold and italic markup does not throw for any retained family.
- `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter 'Invoice_Test|Email_Manager_Test|Payment_Manager_Test'`, `vendor/bin/phpcs` on the changed files, `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse`, and `git diff --check`.
- Measure the packaged size change (`du` of `vendor/mpdf/mpdf/ttfonts/` before and after, and the built ZIP if practical) and record it in the PR. The expected increase is about 1.8 MB uncompressed.
- `composer install --no-dev` still ends with only the intended fonts present.

title: fix: secondary-network setup state duplicates rows and unset-up networks stay half provisioned (follow-up to #2013)
body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #2013 (secondary-network table setup), observed on a production install right after deploying it (2026-10-27 20:42 UTC). Two defects:

### 1. Concurrent first requests insert duplicate `wu_network_table_versions` rows

`Table::maybe_install_network_table()` (`inc/database/engine/class-table.php`) takes the per-network named lock, but `set_network_setup_state()` builds the new state from `get_network_setup_state()`, which reads the **request-start object cache** primed by `Requirements::run_setup()` (`wp_prime_network_option_caches`). It never re-reads the option from the database under the lock. Each concurrent first request therefore sees "option missing" and `update_network_option()` falls through to `add_network_option()`:

```
meta_id  site_id  meta_key                   md5(meta_value)
3816     3        wu_network_table_versions  a32cbc2a…
3817     3        wu_network_table_versions  a32cbc2a…
3818     3        wu_network_table_versions  a32cbc2a…
```

The same stale read lets one request overwrite entries another request just recorded (lost update), which causes tables to be re-checked with DDL locking on later requests.

### 2. Networks without `wu_setup_finished` never get core tables, but still run core queries

Core table classes are only constructed (and so only installed) after `Requirements::run_setup()` returns the network's `wu_setup_finished`. Networks that never ran the setup wizard (on the observed install: networks 4, 5 and 6, where core is loaded through a must-use plugin filter on `site_option_active_sitewide_plugins`) still run front-end code such as `Domain_Mapping\Primary_Domain::redirect_to_primary_domain()` → `wu_get_domains()`. Before #2013 this logged ~1,700 `Table 'wu_6_d' doesn't exist` errors per day; after #2013 the query is silently skipped because `$wpdb->wu_6_domain_mappings` is unregistered. Add-on tables (for example Emails) are still installed on those networks, so a network ends up half set up.

## Fix

1. In `maybe_install_network_table()`, after acquiring the lock, refresh the state from the database (`wp_cache_delete( "{$network_id}:wu_network_table_versions", 'site-options' )` or a direct `SELECT` from `sitemeta`) before checking/recording, and have `set_network_setup_state()` write that fresh state. On read, if more than one row exists for the key, keep the lowest `meta_id` and delete the rest.
2. Decide and implement one consistent behaviour for loaded-but-not-set-up secondary networks: either (a) install core network tables there too (no wizard dependency for schema), or (b) skip front-end features that query network tables (domain mapping redirect, etc.) and skip add-on table installation until `wu_setup_finished` is set. Recommendation: (a), because the plugin is network-active there and its hooks already run.

### Files Scope

- `inc/database/engine/class-table.php`
- `inc/class-requirements.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Database/Engine/Table_Test.php`

## Verification

- Simulate two requests that both prime an empty state, then run setup sequentially in the same process with the primed cache: exactly one `wu_network_table_versions` row exists and it contains both tables' versions.
- A secondary network with `wu_setup_finished` unset: after the first front-end request, either `wp_wu_{N}_domain_mappings` exists (option a) or no network-table query and no add-on table install runs (option b).
- Main network: unchanged query count (`Table_Test` 0-query assertion still passes).

title: fix: CJK invoices blocked by the unsupported-script check (regression from GH#2037)
body:
## Summary

Regression from #2038 (and #2037): invoices that contain Chinese, Japanese or Korean text now fail with *"The invoice contains text the bundled PDF fonts cannot render (Han)"*. Before #2038 they generated a PDF.

## Evidence

Found while reviewing English and mixed-content sample invoices. An English invoice with a Chinese customer name (`王小明` in the billing address) generates on the code before #2038 and fails on `main` after it. In the same run, a Latin invoice and an Arabic-name invoice were pixel-identical before and after.

Cause: `Invoice::get_unsupported_scripts()` asks mPDF's `LanguageToFont` for the font of each script and flags it when that font file is not on disk. With `mode => '+aCJK'` (`useAdobeCJK = true`), mPDF returns its built-in Adobe CJK names, `gb`, `big5`, `sjis` and `uhc`, for Han, Hiragana, Katakana and Hangul. Those are not files and have no `fontdata` entry, so `is_font_available()` returns false. mPDF itself treats them as always available (`in_array($v, ['sjis', 'uhc', 'big5', 'gb'])` in `Mpdf::setCSS`). The docblock added in #2038 claims Adobe CJK scripts are not reported. That is wrong for these names, and the tests added there did not cover CJK.

## Fix

In `Invoice::get_unsupported_scripts()`, treat `sjis`, `uhc`, `big5` and `gb` as available. Do not report them. Correct the docblock. CJK output stays as it was before #2038: the PDF references non-embedded Adobe CJK fonts, which most viewers substitute with a system CJK font. Embedding CJK fonts is out of scope.

## Files

- `inc/invoices/class-invoice.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Invoices/Invoice_Test.php`

Reference: `Invoice::is_font_available()` and the mPDF check in `vendor/mpdf/mpdf/src/Mpdf.php`.

## Verification

- New test: Chinese, Japanese and Korean text return `[]` from `get_unsupported_scripts()`, and `get_content()` returns a PDF.

body:
## Summary

Replace the bundled mPDF fonts for non-Latin invoice PDF scripts with Noto Sans (SIL OFL 1.1), one font per script. This also adds the Indic scripts, Sinhala and Ethiopic, which the bundled fonts could not cover at an acceptable size or licence. Follow-up to #1925, #2037, #2039 and #2045.

## Evidence (spike, rendered through the real `Invoice` class)

- 18 localised invoices were rendered with the Noto set next to mPDF's bundled fonts. The Noto set is clearly better. The bundled FreeSerif has no Indic bold or italic glyphs and shows tofu boxes. Noto renders every style with correct conjuncts and mark placement.
- English, German, French, Spanish, Russian, Greek and Vietnamese invoices are pixel-identical between current `main` and the proposed setup.
- The "Paid" watermark uses DejaVu today, so it shows tofu boxes for every script DejaVu lacks.
- Noto must be adapted for mPDF: stock Noto does not load (unsupported GSUB 5/3, GPOS 8/1 and 8/2 lookups, `MarkGlyphSets`), the 2017 Noto builds load natively for most scripts, and the fonts need ASCII digits, `$` and punctuation (mPDF attaches Common-script characters to the neighbouring script run), overlap removal (the watermark shows overlap artefacts otherwise), and a 1000 units-per-em normalisation.
- Merging scripts into one font breaks mPDF word wrapping (mid-cluster breaks), so each script gets its own font.

## Scope

1. **Fonts:** commit the processed Noto TTFs, regular and bold, under `assets/fonts/noto/`: Devanagari, Bengali, Gujarati, Gurmukhi, Tamil, Malayalam, Oriya, Thaana, Telugu, Kannada, Sinhala, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Hebrew and Ethiopic. Add the OFL text and a provenance notice. Add the build script `scripts/build-invoice-fonts.py` with its inputs documented so the files can be regenerated.
2. **Mapping:** add `WP_Ultimo\Invoices\Language_To_Font` (extends mPDF's `LanguageToFont`) and pass it through mPDF's `languageToFont` config key. mPDF maps eight Indic scripts to the single name `freeserif`, so it must be overridden to use one font per script.
3. **Registration:** register the fonts in `fontdata`, `available_unifonts` **and** `default_available_fonts` (mPDF resets the first from the second during rendering). Use a version suffix in the font names so mPDF's persistent font cache never serves stale data after a font update.

title: Primary-domain redirect should be a 301 by default, filterable
body:
## What

`Primary_Domain::redirect_to_primary_domain()` redirects visitors of a non-primary domain to the site's primary domain with `wp_safe_redirect()`, which defaults to **302 Found**. Make it a **301 Moved Permanently** by default, and let integrators change the status with a filter. No new setting.

## Why

Making a mapped domain primary is a permanent move. A 302 tells search engines to keep the old URL indexed, so old links, emails already sent and ranking signals are not transferred to the new primary domain. Observed on a production multisite: after setting `chefradio.radiostationsnetwork.com` as primary, `https://chefradio.centroitaliaradio.com/some/old/path/?a=1` returned `302` to the same path and query on the new host. The path-preserving behaviour is correct; only the status code is wrong.

## How

- File: `inc/domain-mapping/class-primary-domain.php`, `redirect_to_primary_domain()` (the `wp_safe_redirect(set_url_scheme($new_url))` call, ~line 152).
- Pass an explicit status: `wp_safe_redirect(set_url_scheme($new_url), $status)`.
- Default `$status = 301`, filtered through a new `wu_primary_domain_redirect_status` filter (args: `int $status`, `string $new_url`, `string $current_url`, `Domain $primary_domain`) with the same docblock style as the existing `wu_should_redirect_to_primary_domain` filter (`@since` the next version). Cast the filtered value to int and fall back to 301 unless it is a valid 3xx code (301, 302, 303, 307, 308).
- Do **not** add a settings-page option. Anyone who wants a 302 uses the filter.
- Leave `maybe_redirect_to_mapped_or_network_domain()` (admin/login redirects) unchanged; those are session-scoped, not SEO moves.
- Reference pattern: the `wu_should_redirect_to_primary_domain` filter in the same method.
- Existing tests: `tests/WP_Ultimo/Domain_Mapping/Primary_Domain_Test.php`. Update any assertion that expects the default 302 and add a case for the filter if the file already tests the redirect target.

## Verification

- `vendor/bin/phpcs` on the changed files and the existing `Primary_Domain_Test` pass.
- On a site with a primary mapped domain, `curl -sI https://<non-primary-host>/some/path/?a=1` returns `301` with `Location: https://<primary-host>/some/path/?a=1`.
- Adding `add_filter('wu_primary_domain_redirect_status', fn() => 302)` makes the same request return `302`.

## Context

Found while moving a site between hostnames within one network. Related downstream action: none required. Existing sites get the new status automatically after updating.

title: fix: send payment_received receipt after manual payment confirmation and email verification
body:
## Goal

Send the `payment_received` system email (customer receipt and admin notice) in two cases that currently send nothing:

1. A network admin confirms a pending manual payment.
2. A free signup becomes active after its customer verifies their email address.

## Evidence

Release 2.18.0 smoke test on a fresh dev network at `origin/main` c8b5ffe8 (2026-10-28), with mail captured by Mailpit:

- **Manual payment:** Premium checkout with the Manual gateway left payment #1 and membership #1 pending, as expected. An admin then set the payment to Completed with "Activate membership?" on. The membership became active and the site was published, and "Your site is ready!" was sent. **No `payment_received` email went to the customer or the admin.** Event log rows for this step were `changed payment` and `changed membership` only.
- **Free signup with email verification:** the thank-you page says "a receipt for your purchase has been emailed to you". After the customer followed the verification link, the site went READY and "Your site is ready!" was sent. **No "Your free membership is active" / `payment_received` email was sent.**
- Both paths are unchanged since v2.17.2, so this is long-standing, not a regression.

## How

- `payment_received` fires only from `Payment_Manager::handle_payment_success()` (`inc/managers/class-payment-manager.php:109-219`), which listens to `wu_gateway_payment_processed`.
- `wu_gateway_payment_processed` comes from `Base_Gateway::trigger_payment_processed()` (`inc/gateways/class-base-gateway.php:901`). The checkout calls it for free/trial orders only when email verification is not pending (`inc/checkout/class-checkout.php:1074` and `:1108`). Gateways call it on gateway-confirmed payments.
- Manual confirmation path: `Payment_Edit_Admin_Page::handle_save()` (`inc/admin-pages/class-payment-edit-admin-page.php:1458+`) activates the membership but never triggers payment processed.
- Verification path: `Customer_Manager::maybe_verify_email_address()` / `transition_customer_email_verification()` (`inc/managers/class-customer-manager.php:183`, `:245`) publish the deferred free signup but never trigger payment processed.
- Trigger it once in each path, with the payment's gateway (`wu_get_gateway($payment->get_gateway())`) or the manual/free gateway. Guard against duplicate events, for example by checking whether a `payment_received` event already exists for the payment, so a repeated save or verification can't send twice.

### Files Scope

- `inc/admin-pages/class-payment-edit-admin-page.php`
- `inc/managers/class-customer-manager.php`
- `inc/managers/class-payment-manager.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Managers/Payment_Manager_Test.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Managers/Customer_Manager_Test.php`

## Verification

- `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter 'Payment_Manager_Test|Customer_Manager_Test'`
- `vendor/bin/phpcs` on the changed files.
- Dev site with Mailpit: (1) a manual Premium checkout, then admin Completed + "Activate membership?", sends exactly one customer receipt and one admin notice; (2) a free signup with verification sends "Your free membership is active" once, after verification; (3) re-saving the completed payment sends nothing further.

title: fix: preserve SVN filenames and recover WordPress.org releases

## Problem

Release v2.18.0 was published to GitHub, but its WordPress.org deployment failed before committing trunk. Run: https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite/actions/runs/40619556462

title: Clearer default custom-domain DNS instructions and configurable DNS target
body:
## What

Improve UM's default custom-domain DNS instructions and let network admins set a recommended DNS target, so end customers can map domains correctly without support.

## Why

`Domain_Manager::default_domain_mapping_instructions()` (`inc/managers/class-domain-manager.php`) only says "create a new CNAME record pointing to `%NETWORK_DOMAIN%`". Customers struggle because:

- many DNS providers do not allow a CNAME on the apex; the text gives no A-record fallback even though `%NETWORK_IP%` exists;
- it does not mention the `www` record (UM's `auto_create_www_subdomain` creates it, so it needs DNS too);
- hosts often want customers to point at a dedicated hosting hostname, not the network's main domain; there is no setting for that;
- Cloudflare users get no guidance (proxy on/off, SSL/TLS Full (strict)).

Real case (2026-10-31): a customer on a hosted UM network pointed `www.<their-domain>` at an unrelated domain of theirs and needed operator help; the host had to hand-write instructions per network.

## How

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `inc/managers/class-domain-manager.php` — `default_domain_mapping_instructions()` (rewrite the default text: apex CNAME if the provider supports it, otherwise A to `%NETWORK_IP%`; `www` CNAME; remove conflicting records; Cloudflare note; first HTTPS visit can take a minute while SSL is issued); `get_domain_mapping_instructions()` (add a `%DNS_TARGET%` placeholder); settings registration near the `domain_mapping_instructions` field (~line 800) — add an optional `domain_mapping_dns_target` setting (defaults to the network domain) and document the new placeholder in the field `desc`.
- Keep the `wu_get_domain_mapping_instructions` filter signature backward compatible.

### Hazards

- Stored custom instructions must render unchanged; only the default changes.
- `%NETWORK_IP%` comes from `Domain_Mapping\Helper::get_network_public_ip()`; behind proxies/NAT it can be wrong, so phrase the A record as a fallback and let `domain_mapping_dns_target` take priority.
- All new strings translatable (`ultimate-multisite` text domain).

### Verification

- PHPUnit for `Domain_Manager` if present; otherwise focused test of `get_domain_mapping_instructions()` with: empty setting (new default), custom setting (unchanged), `domain_mapping_dns_target` set (`%DNS_TARGET%` replaced).
- Manual: Network Admin → Settings → Domain Mapping shows the new field; the add-domain modal shows the new default.

### Files Scope

- inc/managers/class-domain-manager.php

## Acceptance Criteria

- Default instructions cover apex CNAME/A fallback, `www`, conflicting records, and Cloudflare.
- Network admins can set a recommended DNS target used by `%DNS_TARGET%` and the default text.
- Existing custom instructions and the filter keep working.

title: Passwordless onboarding: passkey at checkout, password fallback, account emails on the signup site
body:
## Problem

Customers who sign up through checkout get an auto-generated password they never see, and they can't get back into their account. Observed on a production network (2026-10-31):

1. **Wrong-domain links.** The "[Site] Login Details" email from a checkout on a mapped storefront subsite linked to the main network domain's `wp-login.php`. In `inc/checkout/class-checkout-pages.php`, the subsite-aware account-email filters (#1168: `retrieve_password_message`, `wp_new_user_notification_email`, `retrieve_password_notification_email`, `new_user_email_content`) are registered only when `enable_custom_login_page` is on.
2. **No passkey prompt for new customers.** With `use_passwordless_login` on, passkeys are offered only after an email-code login. Customers who sign up at checkout are never asked to create one.
3. **No password option in the inline checkout login.** With passwordless on, `views/checkout/partials/inline-login-prompt.php` replaces the password form entirely, so existing password users can't use their password there (`wp-login.php` keeps a "Use password instead" link).
4. **Welcome email assumes a password.** With passwordless on, it still only says "To set your password, visit…".

## Fix

- Register the account-email filters on every site regardless of the custom login page. Without a custom login page, subsite links use the subsite's own `wp-login.php`; the home-URL rewrite needs the custom login page's handlers.
- With passwordless on, prepend sign-in instructions (email code or passkey, with the login URL) to the welcome email, keeping the set-password link.
- Thank-you page (`wu_thank_you_before_info_blocks`): offer "Create passkey" to the signed-in customer who owns the payment and has no passkey. It uses the existing `wu_passwordless_register_*` endpoints and a new `data-success="stay"` mode in `assets/js/passwordless-auth.js`. Filter: `wu_checkout_offer_passkey`.
- Inline checkout login: keep the password form behind "Use password instead" in passwordless mode.

## Verification

- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Checkout/Checkout_Pages_Test.php`: new tests for filter registration without a custom login page, subsite `wp-login.php` links, passwordless email wording, and passkey prompt conditions/markup. The existing #1168 home-URL tests now enable the custom login page explicitly.
- Manual: enable passwordless, complete a checkout on a mapped subsite, then check the thank-you prompt, the welcome email links, and the inline login password fallback.

title: Passkeys can't be used to sign in: add usernameless passkey sign-in (and fix passwordless email input overflow)
body:
## Problem

Saved passkeys can't be used to sign in. Production test (2026-11-01): a passkey created from the thank-you prompt (#2068) was stored (`wp_wu_passkey_credentials`, active). Entering that email on `wp-login.php` still returned `{"mode":"otp"}` from `wu_passwordless_start` with `supports_webauthn=1`. This is deliberate: `test_ajax_start_does_not_expose_passkey_options_before_otp_verification` keeps the start step from revealing which emails have passkeys. But there's no other passkey path, so the "Use passkey" step is unreachable.

## Fix

Add usernameless (discoverable-credential) passkey sign-in. It doesn't enumerate users:

- `inc/auth/class-passkey-service.php`: `get_discoverable_authentication_options()` creates an `authentication` challenge with `user_id = 0` and empty `allowCredentials`. `verify_authentication()` accepts a challenge with `user_id === 0`, or one equal to the credential's user (the signature then binds the user). Registration options request `residentKey: 'preferred'` so new passkeys are discoverable.
- `inc/auth/class-passwordless-auth-manager.php`: a nopriv AJAX action returns those options. Render a "Sign in with a passkey" button (and optionally conditional mediation, `autocomplete="username webauthn"`) on `wp-login.php`, the login element and the inline checkout prompt. Reuse `ajax_verify_passkey` for verification and redirect.
- `assets/js/passwordless-auth.js`: button handler that fetches discoverable options, then calls `navigator.credentials.get()` and `wu_passwordless_verify_passkey`.

## Also

The email input in the passwordless form overflows the `wp-login.php` form box on the right (seen on ultimatemultisite.com and customer network login pages, 1280px viewport). Add `box-sizing: border-box; max-width: 100%` to `.wu-passwordless-email`.

## Verification

- Unit: discoverable options carry no `allowCredentials` and are bound to no user. Verification works for a discoverable challenge and fails for a challenge bound to another user. Start still returns `otp`.
- Browser: Chromium virtual authenticator (CDP `WebAuthn.addVirtualAuthenticator`, `hasResidentKey: true`): create a passkey from the thank-you prompt, sign out, click "Sign in with a passkey", and land signed in.

title: fix(duplication): site clone fails on tables with generated columns (FluentCRM fc_messages)
body:
## Problem

Creating a site from a template fails on MySQL when the template has a table with a generated column, e.g. FluentCRM's `fc_messages.activity_at`:

```
[ERROR] Got error "The value specified for generated column 'activity_at' in table 'bma_3_fc_messages' is not allowed." while running: INSERT IGNORE `bma_3_fc_messages` SELECT * FROM `bma_2_fc_messages`
[ERROR] Could not copy the complete template database.
```

## Root cause

`MUCD_Data::db_copy_tables()` (`inc/duplication/data.php:168`) recreates each table with `SHOW CREATE TABLE` (so the generated column is preserved) and then copies rows with `INSERT IGNORE dst SELECT * FROM src`. `SELECT *` includes generated columns, and MySQL rejects explicit values for them (error 3105) even with `IGNORE`. `do_sql_query()` records the error and `Site_Duplicator` (`inc/helpers/class-site-duplicator.php:625-627`) fails the clone. MariaDB only emits warning 1906, which is why it is not reproducible there.

## Fix

Read `SHOW COLUMNS` for the source table; when any column's `Extra` is `VIRTUAL|STORED|PERSISTENT GENERATED` (not MySQL 8's `DEFAULT_GENERATED`), copy with an explicit writable column list so the database recomputes generated values. Tables without generated columns keep `SELECT *`.

## Verification

`wp eval-file` against the dev DB with a table containing VIRTUAL + PERSISTENT generated columns and a `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` column: new query copies rows without error, generated values are recomputed, plain tables still use `SELECT *`.

title: Domain mapping: apply primary mapped domain to home_url/site_url for other sites, not only the current request host
body:
## Summary

A site's primary mapped domain is only applied to `home_url` / `site_url` when the **current request's host** is a mapping of that same site. Everywhere else (main site, network admin, "My Sites", cross-site loops calling `get_home_url($blog_id)`, cron, CLI) WordPress returns the raw stored `home`/`siteurl` option, i.e. the site's original network address. If that address is a domain the customer no longer wants, links built from another site send users to the old host, where admin, uploads and REST keep working on the old domain.

## Observed in production (anonymised)

- Site N has `wp_blogs.domain = old.example.com`, mapping A `new.example.net` (`active=1, primary_domain=1`), mapping B `old.example.com` (`active=1, primary_domain=0`). `force_admin_redirect = both`.
- Front end on the old host correctly 301s to the primary (`Primary_Domain::redirect_to_primary_domain`).
- A network-wide SSO/plugin on the main site builds per-site links with `get_home_url($id)` → returns `https://old.example.com` because `mangle_url()` bails when `$site_id` differs from the current request's mapping.
- Editors follow those links, stay in wp-admin on the old host (no admin redirect under `both`), and every upload gets an old-domain URL (43 attachments in a week).
- Only fix was changing the site's network address itself, which defeats the purpose of a primary mapping.

## Root cause

`inc/class-domain-mapping.php`:

- `register_mapped_filters()` (~line 517) registers the URL filters only when `$_SERVER['HTTP_HOST']` matches a mapping, and stores that mapping as `current_mapping`.
- `replace_url()` (~line 612) rewrites to `current_mapping->get_domain()` — the request's mapping, not the site's primary mapping.
- `mangle_url()` (~line 682) returns the URL unchanged when `current_mapping->get_blog_id() !== $site_id`, so other sites are never mapped.

## Proposed change

1. Register `home_url` / `site_url` (with `$blog_id`/`$site_id` args) filters whenever domain mapping is enabled, not only when the request host is mapped.
2. In `mangle_url()`, when there is no current mapping or `$site_id` is a different site, resolve that site's primary mapping via the existing `\WP_Ultimo\Models\Site::get_primary_mapped_domain()` (`inc/models/class-site.php:1334`) and pass it to `replace_url($url, $mapping)` (the second parameter already exists for this). Cache the per-site lookup (existing `domain_mappings` global cache group) so loops over many sites do not add a query per call.
3. Keep current behaviour for the **current** site on a mapped request host (respects `force_admin_redirect = both`, so admin on an alternate mapped domain keeps working).
4. Do not change raw `option_home`/`option_siteurl` reads for other sites unless needed; the `home_url`/`site_url` filters cover `get_home_url()`/`get_site_url()`/`get_admin_url()`.

Optional follow-up (separate PR is fine): when the request host is a non-primary mapping and `force_admin_redirect = force_map`, ensure admin redirects to the primary mapping rather than the request mapping.

### Files Scope

- `inc/class-domain-mapping.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Domain_Mapping_Test.php`

Reference only: `inc/models/class-site.php` (`get_primary_mapped_domain()`) and `inc/domain-mapping/class-primary-domain.php` (redirect behaviour to stay consistent).

## Acceptance / verification

- From the main site context (`wp --url=<main-site> eval 'echo get_home_url(<N>);'`), a site with an active primary mapping returns the primary mapped domain.
- Network admin → Sites list and "My Sites" show the primary mapped domain.
- A site without mappings is unchanged.
- Visiting wp-admin on a non-primary mapped host with `force_admin_redirect = both` still works and keeps that host (no regression).
- No extra DB query per `get_home_url()` call in a loop over sites after the first lookup (object cache hit).
- `vendor/bin/phpcs` clean on changed files; existing PHPUnit suite passes.

## Problem

Customer reports that with **Settings → Login & Registration → Default Role** set to a custom role ("CRM Admin"), new customers are still added to their site as **Administrator**.

## Root cause

The plan editor's **Customer Role** select (`inc/admin-pages/class-product-edit-admin-page.php:757`) uses `Product::get_customer_role()`, which resolves an unset/`default` limit to the *current* global `default_role` (`inc/limitations/class-limit-customer-user-role.php:74`). So "Use Ultimate Multisite default" is never shown as selected; the select shows the resolved role (`administrator` out of the box). Saving the plan then stores that role explicitly, and `Site::save()` (`inc/models/class-site.php:2238-2241`) prefers the plan's role over the global setting from then on. Changing Default Role later has no effect on that plan.

## Fix

Show the stored value in the editor, falling back to `default`, so saving a plan without touching the field keeps following the global setting.

## Verification

Dev network, global Default Role later switched to WooCommerce `shop_manager`, site cloned from template via pending-site publish:
- Plan saved with the old editor value → stored `administrator` → customer gets `administrator`.
- Plan saved with the patched editor value → stored `default` → customer gets `shop_manager`.

Existing plans that already have an explicit role keep it; the editor now displays it so admins can switch to "Use Ultimate Multisite default".

title: Race in Cron scheduling creates duplicate recurring chains (wu_membership_check / wu_hourly run twice per hour)
body:
**Summary**
wu_membership_check and wu_hourly end up scheduled as two independent recurring chains, so both run twice per hour (48 completed actions per day instead of 24). Each chain reschedules itself, so the duplicate never goes away on its own. Because async_create_renewal_payment() is check-then-create, a duplicate run can in rare cases create two renewal payments (and two renewal_payment_created emails) for the same membership.

**Environment**
Ultimate Multisite 2.18.0 (also seen on 2.17.2), WordPress 7.1.4 multisite, PHP 8.5
Action Scheduler 4.1.0 (loaded from WooCommerce 11.2.1)
Redis object cache
DISABLE_WP_CRON = true; a system cron runs wp cron event run --due-now for each site every minute; Action Scheduler async requests are also active
What we see
Tools → Scheduled Actions on the main site, group wu_cron:

two pending wu_membership_check actions with the same scheduled time;
two pending wu_hourly actions a few minutes apart;
for at least a week: 48 completed wu_hourly and 48 completed wu_membership_check per day.
After cancelling one pending copy of each, a single chain continues normally.

**Cause**
Cron::schedule_membership_check() and Cron::schedule_recurring_hook_when_needed() run on every init and do check-then-schedule:

if (wu_next_scheduled_action('wu_membership_check') === false) {
    wu_schedule_recurring_action(time(), $interval, 'wu_membership_check', [], 'wu_cron');
}
When a recurring action finishes, Action Scheduler marks it complete and only then inserts the next instance. A request that hits init in that window (or two concurrent requests on a fresh install) sees nothing scheduled and starts a second chain. wu_schedule_recurring_action() / wu_enqueue_async_action() do not pass the $unique argument, and nothing else guards against this.

**Impact**
membership_renewal_check() and membership_trial_check() enqueue wu_async_create_renewal_payment once per run. With two runs per hour, the same membership gets two async actions. async_create_renewal_payment() checks get_last_pending_payment() and then creates a payment without a lock. If the two actions are processed at the same moment (WP-Cron runner and async-request runner), two renewal payments and two "renewal payment created" emails can be produced.
The expiring notice is already safe: async_membership_expiring() records the notice meta before firing the event.
Duplicate demo-site checks (wu_hourly) and doubled load and log entries.

**Suggested fix**
Pass $unique = true in the scheduler wrappers: for the recurring wu_cron hooks, and for per-membership async actions such as wu_async_create_renewal_payment (unique per hook + args). Action Scheduler 3.6+ supports this.
Don't (re)schedule on every init. Schedule on activation/upgrade and self-check from admin or cron context, or guard the check-and-schedule with a short lock.
Make async_create_renewal_payment() safe under concurrency, for example with a per-membership lock around "no pending payment → create payment", like async_membership_expiring() already does for notices.
Optionally self-heal: on action_scheduler_begin_execute for a wu_cron recurring action, cancel other pending copies with the same hook, args and group.

**Workaround**
Cancel the extra pending wu_membership_check / wu_hourly action in Tools → Scheduled Actions.

title: fix(site): saving a site with a failed template clone silently re-clones it and erases the site's content
body:
## Problem (data loss, reproduced on `main` @ 98fa74b0 and in every release since v2.17.0)

When a template clone fails, any later `Site::save()` on that site silently re-clones the template over it and destroys everything built on the site since the failure. A customer network reported this: they rebuilt a customer site three times and each time it "rolled back to the template" without them doing anything; the site also showed "This site has been archived or suspended".

### Sequence

1. **Network Admin → Sites → Add Site** with a template. `MUCD_Data::copy_data()` records any SQL error (for example the MySQL generated-column error fixed for the next release in #2075/#2078). `Site_Duplicator::process_duplication()` (`inc/helpers/class-site-duplicator.php:625-628`) returns `site_clone_database_failed` ("Could not copy the complete template database."). The blog already exists, so `Site::save()` (`inc/models/class-site.php` ~L2020-2030) recovers the blog ID and saves the `wu_site` record anyway. The site is left with `wu_clone_status=failed` and **`archived=1`** (set at L590 and only restored on success). That archived flag is the "archived or suspended" front-end message.
2. The super admin can still open wp-admin for an archived site, so they build the customer's site there.
3. **Any** later `Site::save()` on an existing site goes through the `else` branch at `inc/models/class-site.php:2095-2117`. Because `wu_clone_status === 'failed'` and a template ID is set, it calls `Site_Duplicator::duplicate_site(..., ['to_site_id' => $this->get_id()])`. `db_copy_tables()` then **DROPs and recreates every table** from the template. Callers that reach this include:
   - Edit Site → attach membership/customer (`inc/admin-pages/class-site-edit-admin-page.php:285`). This produced the customer's "error moving database to new member", and everything was erased.
   - `Site_Manager::async_get_site_screenshot()` (`inc/managers/class-site-manager.php:748-767`). This is scheduled 90 seconds after creation and calls `$site->save()` with no user action ("I didn't even do anything").
   - `wu_update_site`/membership sync paths (`inc/functions/site.php:358`, `inc/managers/class-membership-manager.php:1147`, `inc/managers/class-site-manager.php:1844`).
4. If the copy error persists (it does, until the root cause is fixed), every save wipes the tables again, returns the same error and leaves the site archived.

### Reproduction (PHPUnit, MySQL 8.4 container)

Inject one failing query during the first clone with `add_filter('query', ...)`. Then create a post on the destination, call `wu_get_site($id)->set_featured_image_id(123); ->save()` and check the destination posts table:

```text
[1] create: ERROR Could not copy the complete template database. | status=failed archived=1 wu_site=yes
[3] save: ok | customer post DELETED | tagline='' status=complete archived=0
[4] save w/ persisting error: ERROR Could not copy the complete template database. | customer post DELETED archived=1
```

## Expected

A failed clone must never be re-run implicitly by an unrelated model save. Content created on the site after a failure must survive any save.

## Suggested fix (worker to confirm against callers)

- `inc/models/class-site.php` (existing-site branch ~L2095): remove the implicit `failed → duplicate_site()` retry from `save()`. Keep the `copying` guard.
- Provide an **explicit** retry path instead, e.g. `Site::retry_failed_clone()` or a duplication-argument flag, invoked only from a deliberate admin action (Edit Site / Sites list row action "Retry template copy", with a confirm that it overwrites the site). Check whether checkout or pending-site publishing (`Membership_Manager`, `Checkout_Provisioning`) relied on the implicit retry. If so, route it through the explicit method.
- Consider whether a manual Add Site that returns `site_clone_database_failed` should surface the site as failed in the UI (a notice on the Sites list or Edit Site page), so admins don't build on a half-copied archived site.
- Pattern to follow for clone status handling: `Site_Duplicator::get_clone_status()` / `is_clone_failed()` (`inc/helpers/class-site-duplicator.php:62-84`). Existing coverage to extend: `tests/WP_Ultimo/Helpers/Site_Clone_Lifecycle_Test.php` (`test_failed_initializer_keeps_destination_quarantined`).

## Verification

- New regression test in `tests/WP_Ultimo/Models/` (or extend `Site_Clone_Lifecycle_Test`): failed clone → write a post on destination → `wu_get_site($id)->save()` → post still exists, no tables dropped, no `site-duplication` log entry for a retry.
- Explicit retry path still re-clones and clears `archived` on success (the existing `test_failed_initializer_keeps_destination_quarantined` assertions).
- `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter 'Site_Clone_Lifecycle_Test|Site_Duplicator_Test|Site_Test'`, `vendor/bin/phpcs`, `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse` on touched files.

## Related

- Root cause seen most often for the first failure on MySQL: generated columns (FluentCRM `fc_messages`). Fixed on `main` in #2075 / #2078, **not yet released** (latest release v2.18.0).
- Implicit retry introduced in eb9ee5ac ("feat(cloning): own template initialization and readiness", v2.17.0).

body:
## Problem

Since v2.17.0 (eb9ee5ac, "feat(cloning): own template initialization and readiness"), the first SQL error anywhere in `MUCD_Data::copy_data()` fails the whole template clone. The error is captured in `MUCD_Data::do_sql_query()` (`inc/duplication/data.php`) and checked in `Site_Duplicator::process_duplication()` (`inc/helpers/class-site-duplicator.php`). The site is then archived, with the generic message "Could not copy the complete template database."

Every query counts the same, including errors on plugin tables and on single rows in the URL search-replace pass. A customer network's templates copied successfully for months; after updating to 2.17+, every copy from those templates fails and the site is archived. When unarchived, the sites look complete, which fits a non-essential error that earlier versions logged and ignored. The admin also can't tell which table failed without finding the separate `site-duplication-errors` log.

Fully reverting to "ignore all errors" would bring back the original problem: sites handed to customers with a missing `posts` or `options` table.

## Proposed fix: two tiers

- **Fatal** (behaviour as now: failed status, archived, retry offered):
  - reading the template's table list fails, or
  - creating or filling a core WordPress per-site table (`$wpdb->tables`: posts, postmeta, options, terms, term_taxonomy, term_relationships, termmeta, comments, commentmeta, links) fails.
- **Warning** (the clone completes and the site goes live):
  - plugin tables, and
  - the URL replacement pass.
  - Record the failures per table in destination-owned site meta, log them, and show them in an Edit Site notice.
- The fatal message names the failing table; the MySQL error goes only to the `site-duplication` log, because the message can reach customers at checkout.
- Add a filter `wu_mucd_copy_error_is_fatal` so a network can make a plugin table required or optional.

## Verification

- New tests: a plugin table failure completes with a warning; a core table failure is fatal and names the table without the MySQL detail; the filter makes a plugin table fatal; a URL replacement failure is a warning; a clean clone records no warnings.
- Existing duplication, site, Edit Site and provisioning suites still pass.

Related: #2104 / #2105 (failed clones were re-copied on save).

title: fix: addon-integration-test PHPUnit step silently skipped ([[ under sh)
body:
## Problem

The shared `addon-integration-test.yml` workflow never runs addon PHPUnit suites. The "Run addon PHPUnit tests" step uses bash `[[ … ]]`, but in the `cimg/php` job container it runs under `sh -e`, so the test fails with `[[: not found`, falls through to the `else` branch, prints "No phpunit.xml.dist found — skipping PHPUnit", and exits 0. Every addon that calls this workflow reports a green PHPUnit job without executing any tests.

## Evidence

A private addon's CI, job "integration-test / PHPUnit (PHP 8.3)" (2026-11-17):

```
shell: sh -e {0}
No phpunit.xml.dist found — skipping PHPUnit
/__w/_temp/….sh: 1: [[: not found
/__w/_temp/….sh: 1: [[: not found
```

That addon does ship `phpunit.xml.dist`. A local run of its suite shows real failures that CI never reported.

## Proposed fix

- In `.github/workflows/addon-integration-test.yml`, step "Run addon PHPUnit tests": either add `shell: bash`, or switch to POSIX `[ -f phpunit.xml.dist ] || [ -f phpunit.xml ]`. Check the other `run:` steps in the same workflow for bash-only syntax too.
- Rollout: once tests actually run, some addon suites will turn red. Land this together with a note to addon maintainers, or temporarily allow failures (`continue-on-error`) for a short burn-in, so the regression is visible without blocking unrelated PRs.

### Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/addon-integration-test.yml`

## Verification

1. Re-run any addon PR that calls this workflow. The PHPUnit job log must show `PHPUnit 9.x` and a `Tests: N` summary, with no `[[: not found`.
2. An addon without `phpunit.xml.dist` must still log the skip message.
