title: Cloudflare Custom Hostnames ignore the auto_create_www_subdomain setting for mapped domains
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `cloudflare custom hostname www` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 commits / 0 merged PRs / 0 open PRs touch the target files in the last 48h (keyword hits #195, merged 2025-09, and #2073, open, concern other files)
- [x] File refs verified: 5 files compared by blob hash against the remote default branch; every cited line re-read
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — disqualifier check clean (verified reference pattern in the same file; no unresolved design decision)
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the change is small and the reference pattern is cited inline

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-18
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (requested by the maintainer)
- **Parent task:** none
- **Conversation context:** Found while answering a support question about Cloudflare for SaaS (Custom Hostnames) on a subdirectory network. Reading `Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping::on_add_domain()` showed it registers only the hostname exactly as saved on the domain record, unlike other integrations.

## What

When the Cloudflare integration has a Custom Hostnames Zone ID (`WU_CLOUDFLARE_SAAS_ZONE_ID`), mapping `example.com` must also register `www.example.com` as a Custom Hostname whenever `Domain_Manager::should_create_www_subdomain()` returns true (setting `auto_create_www_subdomain`: `always` is the default, plus `main_only` and `never`). Removing the mapped domain must remove both hostnames. With `never`, with a saved domain that already starts with `www.`, or without a SaaS zone ID, behaviour stays exactly as it is today.

## Why

The setting's own tooltip says it "applies to all hosting integrations" (`inc/managers/class-domain-manager.php:849`), and several integrations honour it for mapped domains (for example Plesk, ServerPilot, Hestia, WPMU DEV, DirectAdmin and Cloudways). The Cloudflare Custom Hostnames path does not: `on_add_domain()` makes a single POST for the saved hostname. Domain mapping itself matches both `example.com` and `www.example.com` (`get_www_and_nowww_versions()`, `inc/class-domain-mapping.php:341`), so a customer who points `www` at the Cloudflare fallback origin reaches a hostname that has no Custom Hostname, and an admin has to add a second domain record by hand.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The reference pattern is in the same file (`on_add_subdomain()`, `:749-760`, filter `wu_cloudflare_should_add_www`) and in other integrations. The decisions (reuse that filter, continue after a per-hostname failure, skip quietly on remove) are made below, but the worker still shapes the refactor and the test updates.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php:596-715` — `on_add_domain()` (create) and `on_remove_domain()` (delete) handle the apex and, when allowed, the `www.` variant.
- `EDIT: tests/WP_Ultimo/Integrations/Providers/Cloudflare/Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping_Test.php:74-148` — existing `on_add_domain` / `on_remove_domain` tests. `test_on_add_domain_calls_api_when_saas_zone_id_set` asserts exactly one API call (`expects($this->once())`) and will see two under the default setting.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `wu_add_domain` / `wu_remove_domain` hooks registered at `class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php:82-83`; fired through Action Scheduler from `Domain_Manager::send_domain_to_host()` (`inc/managers/class-domain-manager.php:1021-1056`) and `handle_domain_deleted()` (`:666-680`).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** Cloudflare API calls through `Cloudflare_Integration::cloudflare_api_call()`: `POST client/v4/zones/{zone}/custom_hostnames`, `GET .../custom_hostnames?hostname=`, `DELETE .../custom_hostnames/{id}`.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping_Test.php` mocks `cloudflare_api_call` and `get_credential`; no other test targets these handlers (`rg -n "custom_hostnames" tests`).
- **Schemas/config:** setting `auto_create_www_subdomain` (`class-domain-manager.php:843-861`, default `always`); filters `wu_cloudflare_custom_hostname_data` (`class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php:617`, keep its signature) and `wu_cloudflare_should_add_www` (`:749`, reuse).
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** N/A — no new translatable strings (log lines go through `wu_log_add` and are untranslated), so `lang/ultimate-multisite.pot` is unchanged.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because domains mapped before this change keep their single Custom Hostname and no backfill is performed.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `on_remove_domain()` deletes both hostnames when a domain is removed; rollback of the change itself is a plain revert, and hostnames already created stay in Cloudflare until their domain is removed.

### Implementation Steps

1. In `on_add_domain()`, after the SaaS zone check, build the hostname list, mirroring `on_add_subdomain()`:

   ```php
   $hostnames = [$domain];

   $should_add_www = apply_filters(
   	'wu_cloudflare_should_add_www',
   	\WP_Ultimo\Managers\Domain_Manager::get_instance()->should_create_www_subdomain($domain),
   	$domain,
   	$site_id
   );

   if ( ! str_starts_with($domain, 'www.') && $should_add_www) {
   	$hostnames[] = 'www.' . $domain;
   }
   ```

2. Loop over `$hostnames`. Build `$data` with the existing `wu_cloudflare_custom_hostname_data` filter (pass the loop hostname as the `$domain` argument), POST it, and log success or failure per hostname. A failure on one hostname must `continue`, not `return`, so the other is still attempted.
3. In `on_remove_domain()`, keep the existing lookup and delete for the saved hostname, then repeat it for `'www.' . $domain` when the saved domain does not start with `www.`. When the `www.` lookup finds nothing, skip quietly (log at info level, not `LogLevel::WARNING`): the domain may have been added while the setting was `never`.
4. Update `test_on_add_domain_calls_api_when_saas_zone_id_set` (set `auto_create_www_subdomain` to `never` for the single-call case, or expect two calls) and add one small case proving the `www.` hostname is posted by default and not posted under `never`. Leave the "skips when no SaaS zone id" tests unchanged.
5. Do not change method signatures: `on_add_domain(string $domain, int $site_id): void` and `on_remove_domain(...)` already declare `void`. Add-ons extend integration classes, so do not add return types to other public methods.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** the two API calls are independent; one can succeed while the other fails. Each failure is logged per hostname and never thrown.
- **Migration/rollback:** none; only future mappings and removals are affected.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** `wu_cloudflare_custom_hostname_data` keeps its signature `($data, $domain, $site_id)` but now runs once per hostname; say so in the filter's docblock. Code that filters by hostname keeps working.
- **Idempotency/retry:** `wu_add_domain` runs as an Action Scheduler job and can be retried. Cloudflare rejects duplicate hostnames, which surfaces as a logged `WP_Error` exactly as it does for the apex today.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** an apex success with a `www.` failure leaves the apex working; the log line names the failed hostname so an admin can add it manually.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
npm test -- --filter Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping_Test
bash -c 'vendor/bin/phpcs inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php tests/WP_Ultimo/Integrations/Providers/Cloudflare/Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping_Test.php'
git diff --check
```

- **Surface mapping:** `npm test -- --filter` forwards to `vendor/bin/phpunit` and proves the add and remove handlers and the setting matrix in `Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping_Test`; phpcs proves WordPress coding standards on both files; `git diff --check` catches whitespace errors. PHPStan runs from the repository pre-commit hook on the staged PHP files.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — the change is confined to one integration class and its test.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not touch the legacy `inc/integrations/host-providers/class-cloudflare-host-provider.php` (its `on_add_domain()` is intentionally empty); do not change the SSL method or type in the Custom Hostname payload; do not add settings, UI or custom-origin options; do not regenerate `lang/ultimate-multisite.pot`.

**AI brief owner:** the maintainer's interactive session that filed this issue.

### Files Scope

- `inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Integrations/Providers/Cloudflare/Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping_Test.php`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a SaaS zone ID set and `auto_create_www_subdomain` at its default (`always`), `on_add_domain('example.com', 1)` posts two `custom_hostnames` payloads (`example.com` and `www.example.com`), and `on_remove_domain('example.com', 1)` deletes both when both exist.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "npm test -- --filter Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping_Test"
  ```

- [ ] Regression guard: with the setting at `never`, with a saved domain that already starts with `www.`, or with no SaaS zone ID, behaviour is unchanged (one POST, one POST and zero API calls respectively), and a missing `www.` hostname on removal logs no WARNING.

- [ ] `vendor/bin/phpcs` on the two changed files is clean.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "vendor/bin/phpcs inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php tests/WP_Ultimo/Integrations/Providers/Cloudflare/Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping_Test.php"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- Reusing `wu_cloudflare_should_add_www` (already applied to network subdomains in `on_add_subdomain()`) avoids a new public hook and keeps one place to veto `www.` for Cloudflare.
- A `www.` Custom Hostname stays pending in Cloudflare until the customer also points `www` at the fallback origin. That matches how other integrations add `www.` aliases and is controlled by the existing setting.
- Companion issue: the explainer wording for this integration on subdirectory networks is tracked separately and is not part of this change.

## Relevant Files

- `inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php:609-715` — handlers to change; `:728-788` — reference pattern in `on_add_subdomain()`.
- `inc/managers/class-domain-manager.php:871-894` — `should_create_www_subdomain()` semantics (`always`, `main_only`, `never`; returns false for a `www.` input).
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Integrations/Providers/Cloudflare/Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping_Test.php:74-148` — existing tests to update.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-18
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (requested by the maintainer)
- **Parent task:** none
- **Conversation context:** Found while answering a support question about Cloudflare for SaaS (Custom Hostnames) on a subdirectory network. The integration screen contradicts itself on subdirectory installs when a Custom Hostnames Zone ID is set.

## What

On a subdirectory network, the Cloudflare integration's explainer must stop claiming the whole integration "has no effect" when a Custom Hostnames Zone ID (`WU_CLOUDFLARE_SAAS_ZONE_ID`) is configured. The "Do nothing!" line is shown only when nothing will actually happen: subdirectory install and no Zone ID. Subdomain installs and the Custom Hostnames lines are unchanged.

## Why

With `WU_CLOUDFLARE_SAAS_ZONE_ID` set on a subdirectory network, the integration wizard lists under "will" both "Do nothing! The CloudFlare integration has no effect in subdirectory multisite installs such as this one" (`inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php:60-64`) and "Register custom domains as Cloudflare Custom Hostnames, ..." (`:68-69`). Custom Hostname registration is not gated by install type: `on_add_domain()` (`:609-647`) only checks for the zone ID, and `Domain_Manager::send_domain_to_host()` enqueues `wu_add_domain` on every install type. The first line is therefore wrong and tells admins the integration is inactive when it is not.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The exact edit is supplied, but which line to show for each combination of install type and zone ID is a small admin-facing wording decision, so the worker also confirms the rendered result; no design decision beyond that remains.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php:60-64` — gate the subdirectory line on the absence of a Custom Hostnames Zone ID.
- `EDIT: tests/WP_Ultimo/Integrations/Providers/Cloudflare/Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping_Test.php:34-43` — extend the existing explainer test file with one focused case (the file already mocks `get_credential`).

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `Integration::get_explainer_lines()` merges module lines (`inc/integrations/class-integration.php:614-626`); `Hosting_Integration_Wizard_Admin_Page` passes `will` and `will_not` to `views/wizards/host-integrations/activation.php` (`inc/admin-pages/class-hosting-integration-wizard-admin-page.php:250-259`; the view guards `will_not` with `! empty()` at `:54`).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** only the array returned by `Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping::get_explainer_lines()`.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping_Test::test_get_explainer_lines_has_will_and_will_not_keys` (`:34-43`) asserts only that both keys exist.
- **Schemas/config:** reads credential `WU_CLOUDFLARE_SAAS_ZONE_ID` through `$this->get_cloudflare()->get_credential()`; no config change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** the edit keeps the existing `__()` string and adds no lines, so `lang/ultimate-multisite.pot` (string and `#:` line references) is unchanged. The legacy `inc/integrations/host-providers/class-cloudflare-host-provider.php:851` carries the same sentence, but that class has no Custom Hostnames support (its `on_add_domain()` is empty), so its wording stays accurate and is out of scope.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the change only affects display text returned by one method and stores no data.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** a plain revert of the edit in `get_explainer_lines()` restores the previous text; nothing else is written.

### Implementation Steps

1. In `get_explainer_lines()` replace the final `else` of the install-type check with an `elseif` on the zone ID. Do not add lines, so the existing string keeps its line number:

   oldString:

   ```php
   		} else {
   			$explainer_lines['will']['subdirectory'] = __('Do nothing! The CloudFlare integration has no effect in subdirectory multisite installs such as this one', 'ultimate-multisite');
   		}
   ```

   newString:

   ```php
   		} elseif ( ! $this->get_cloudflare()->get_credential('WU_CLOUDFLARE_SAAS_ZONE_ID')) {
   			$explainer_lines['will']['subdirectory'] = __('Do nothing! The CloudFlare integration has no effect in subdirectory multisite installs such as this one', 'ultimate-multisite');
   		}
   ```

2. Result by case: subdomain install — unchanged; subdirectory without a zone ID — unchanged ("Do nothing!" plus the existing "will not" lines); subdirectory with a zone ID — the "Do nothing!" line disappears and `will` contains only the Custom Hostnames line added by the existing check at `:68-69`.
3. Add one focused test next to `test_get_explainer_lines_has_will_and_will_not_keys`: stub `get_credential` to return a zone ID for `WU_CLOUDFLARE_SAAS_ZONE_ID`, call `get_explainer_lines()`, and assert `will` has `custom_hostnames` and does not have `subdirectory`. If the test environment is a subdomain install, `is_subdomain_install()` takes the first branch and the assertion on `subdirectory` still holds; keep the assertion on `custom_hostnames` so the test is meaningful either way.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** N/A — pure function of the install type and one credential, no shared state.
- **Migration/rollback:** none; plain revert restores the old text.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** the return shape (`will`, `will_not` string lists keyed by id) is unchanged; add-ons that read explainer lines see the same keys, minus the `subdirectory` key in the one case that was wrong.
- **Idempotency/retry:** the method is called on every render and has no side effects.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if the credential lookup returns an empty value the previous behaviour is preserved.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
npm test -- --filter Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping_Test
bash -c 'vendor/bin/phpcs inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php tests/WP_Ultimo/Integrations/Providers/Cloudflare/Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping_Test.php'
git diff --stat
```

- **Surface mapping:** `npm test -- --filter` forwards to `vendor/bin/phpunit` and proves the explainer arrays for the zone-ID case; phpcs proves coding standards on both files; `git diff --stat` shows the edit stays inside the two scoped files and leaves `lang/ultimate-multisite.pot` untouched. PHPStan runs from the pre-commit hook on staged PHP files.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — one method in one integration class plus its test.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not edit `inc/integrations/host-providers/class-cloudflare-host-provider.php`; do not add or change any translatable string; do not regenerate `lang/ultimate-multisite.pot`; do not change `on_add_domain()` behaviour (a companion issue covers its `www.` handling).

**AI brief owner:** the maintainer's interactive session that filed this issue.

### Files Scope

- `inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Integrations/Providers/Cloudflare/Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping_Test.php`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a Custom Hostnames Zone ID set, `get_explainer_lines()['will']` lists the `custom_hostnames` entry and omits the `subdirectory` entry, whatever the install type.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "npm test -- --filter Cloudflare_Domain_Mapping_Test"
  ```

- [ ] Regression guard: with no Zone ID the lines are exactly as before (subdirectory install keeps "Do nothing!" and the `will_not` entries; subdomain install keeps the proxied-subdomain line), and the string `Do nothing! The CloudFlare integration has no effect in subdirectory multisite installs such as this one` still appears exactly once in the file at the same line.

  ```yaml
    method: codebase
    pattern: "Do nothing! The CloudFlare integration has no effect in subdirectory multisite installs such as this one"
    path: "inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php"
  ```

- [ ] `vendor/bin/phpcs` on the two changed files is clean, and `git diff --stat` shows no change to `lang/ultimate-multisite.pot`.

## Context & Decisions

- Showing nothing (rather than a new "will not add subdomains" line) in the subdirectory-with-zone-ID case avoids adding a translatable string and a `.pot` update for a display nit.
- The legacy host-provider class keeps its sentence because it genuinely does nothing on subdirectory installs.

- `inc/integrations/providers/cloudflare/class-cloudflare-domain-mapping.php:53-75` — method to change.
- `views/wizards/host-integrations/activation.php:54-64` — how the lists are rendered.

title: security(sso): apply mapped-domain token policy to admin-bar magic links
body:
## Problem

Follow-up to GHSA-qh2w-5cww-9wxr (fixed in 2.19.0 by #2119). Admin-bar magic links still send network admins to customer mapped domains with a login token in the URL. Whoever controls the domain's DNS can capture the token and replay it for a network admin session.

An attacker cannot force this: the link needs a nonce-protected click by the admin. But the customer still receives a network-wide credential whenever an admin visits their site this way.

## Files

- `inc/sso/class-admin-bar-magic-links.php`: around line 184, access is allowed for `is_super_admin() || is_user_member_of_blog()`.

- Customer mapped domains: no token for users with `is_super_admin()` / `manage_network`. Non-admins must be members of the site.

Options: make that check reusable (public or a shared helper) and apply it when magic links are generated and redeemed. When a network admin targets a customer mapped domain, send them to that domain's login page instead of minting a token.

title: WooCommerce Subscriptions compat reads new site options before the site's tables exist (wp_insert_site)
body:
## Problem

When a site is created with `wp_insert_site()` (for example from WP-CLI), `Domain_Manager::handle_site_created()` runs on the `wp_insert_site` action and creates the primary domain record. That fires `wu_domain_became_primary`, and `WooCommerce_Subscriptions_Compat::reset_staging_mode_on_primary_domain_change()` calls `switch_to_blog()` and `get_option()` on the new site. This happens **before** WordPress runs `wp_initialize_site`, so the site's tables do not exist yet. On production (2026-11-21, new site 362) this logged a series of `Table '..._362_options' doesn't exist` errors for `wp_362_user_roles`, the `wpdb_wu_*_version` BerlinDB options and `wc_subscriptions_siteurl`. Any option written by `reset_staging_mode()` at that point is silently lost.

Call chain seen: `wp_insert_site` → `Domain_Manager->handle_site_created` → `create_domain_record_for_site` → `wu_create_domain` → `Domain->save` → `do_action('wu_domain_became_primary')` → `WooCommerce_Subscriptions_Compat->reset_staging_mode_on_primary_domain_change` → `reset_staging_mode` → `switch_to_blog` / `get_option`.

## Fix

In `inc/compat/class-woocommerce-subscriptions-compat.php`, skip or defer `reset_staging_mode()` when the target site is not initialized yet (`wp_is_site_initialized( $blog_id )` is false), for example by re-queueing it on `wp_initialize_site` at a late priority. Alternatively, make `Domain_Manager::handle_site_created()` create the domain record on `wp_initialize_site` instead of `wp_insert_site`. Check other `wu_domain_became_primary` listeners for the same assumption.

### Files Scope
- EDIT: `inc/compat/class-woocommerce-subscriptions-compat.php`
- EDIT: `inc/managers/class-domain-manager.php` (only if moving the hook)

## Verification

- `wp eval 'wp_insert_site(["domain"=>"um-test-".time().".example.test","path"=>"/","network_id"=>1,"title"=>"t","user_id"=>1]);'` on a multisite with WooCommerce Subscriptions compat loaded: no "doesn't exist" database errors in the output or debug.log.
- After creation, `wc_subscriptions_siteurl` on the new site matches the value `reset_staging_mode()` is meant to set.
- Existing primary-domain changes on initialized sites still reset staging mode (regression).

title: Domain mapping fix_srcset applies the request's mapped domain to other sites' images after switch_to_blog
body:
## Problem

`Domain_Mapping::fix_srcset()` (`inc/class-domain-mapping.php`, hooked on `wp_calculate_image_srcset`) rewrites every srcset URL with `replace_url()` using `$this->current_mapping`, the mapping of the **request's** host. Unlike `mangle_url()`, which returns early when `$current_mapping->get_blog_id() !== get_current_blog_id()`, `fix_srcset()` has no site check.

So when a request for mapped site A calls `switch_to_blog(B)` and renders B's images, B's srcset URLs get A's domain (`https://site-a.example/app/uploads/sites/B/...`), while `src` stays correct. On a production network (2026-11-21) this was cached in Elementor's `_elementor_element_cache` for four posts of one site. A CDN page-URL rewriter then replaced only the upload path, leaving A's host in front of the CDN URL (`https://site-a.examplehttps://cdn.example/...`), so the logo, banners and product images failed to load on every page of site B.

## Fix

In `fix_srcset()`, return `$sources` unchanged unless `$this->current_mapping->get_blog_id() === get_current_blog_id()`, matching `mangle_url()`. Optionally, use the mapping for the current blog instead of returning early. Check the other filters registered in `register_mapped_filters()` for the same missing guard.

### Files Scope
- EDIT: `inc/class-domain-mapping.php` (`fix_srcset()`, around line 705)

## Verification

- On a multisite with a mapped domain for site A, request A's front end with code that runs `switch_to_blog(B); echo wp_get_attachment_image($id_on_B, 'full'); restore_current_blog();`. Before the fix, srcset URLs use A's domain; after it, they use B's own URLs.
- Regression: images rendered on A itself still get A's mapped domain in srcset.

title: Decide: should confirming a manual payment renew an active membership?
body:
## Decision needed

Should confirming a pending payment renew an *active* manual membership?

Source: review comment on PR #2133 by @coderabbitai. Not a defect in that PR; `main` behaves the same way.

## Premise check

Correct. An administrator cannot renew an active manually billed membership by confirming its payment in the UI. The "Activate Membership?" toggle in the payment editor is hidden when the membership is `active` or `trialing`, so the renewal branch of `handle_save()` is never reached from the page for those memberships.

- Toggle visibility: `inc/admin-pages/class-payment-edit-admin-page.php`, the `confirm_membership` field's `v-if` (around line 1193).
- Renewal branch: `handle_save()` in the same file calls `$membership->renew(false, Membership_Status::ACTIVE)` for a non-initial payment.
- The branch works when `confirm_membership` is posted: the `active renewal` row of `Payment_Edit_Admin_Page_Test::test_manual_confirmation_period` passes.
- On `main` the toggle is shown for `pending` memberships only, so this is not new.

## Analysis

- Manual-gateway renewal payments are created by an administrator (`inc/admin-pages/class-payment-list-admin-page.php:208` and `:461`). Nothing creates them at expiry. The only automatic creators are the Stripe and PayPal webhooks and the migrator.
- Showing the toggle for active memberships would let one confirmation extend the plan's period by a billing cycle. If the administrator has also moved the expiration by hand, that extends it twice.
- A pending payment is not necessarily a renewal. An administrator can create one with custom line items for something else, and confirming it with the toggle on would still renew. The cart type that identifies add-ons and upgrades is stored only for payments created by checkout, so it cannot tell these apart.
- Add-on payments already lift a hold without extending the period (#2133), so any new rule must keep that.

## Recommended path

Keep today's behaviour and document that an active manual membership is extended by editing its expiration. If maintainers want one-click renewal, show the toggle for an active membership only when the payment has a plan line item, and require the administrator to confirm the new expiration date in the same form.

## Verification, if this is built

- A pending payment with a plan line item on an active membership: the toggle appears, confirming extends the expiration by one cycle exactly once, and a repeated save does not extend again.
- A pending payment with only custom line items: no toggle.
- Existing rows of `test_manual_confirmation_period` keep passing.

title: Decide: a magic link shown as plain URL text can be fetched by WordPress and burn its single-use token
body:
## Decision needed

A magic link shown in the "Plain URL Text" display mode (`display_as="url"`) can be fetched by WordPress itself while the page renders. That consumes the single-use token, so the customer's later click fails. How should that be prevented?

Found while re-verifying the account area after #2133. Not caused by it: neither file below changed there.

## Premise check

Correct, reproduced on a block theme with a page containing only `[wu_magic_link_url display_as="url"]`.

Evidence, in order:

1. The page render generated a token bound to the browser's user agent. The server's own request log shows a request for that exact URL 23 seconds later, with the user agent `WordPress/<version>; <site url>` (the WordPress HTTP API), which followed the 301 to a 200. The browser's use of the link came after it.
2. The `magic-link` log then reads `User agent mismatch. Expected: <browser UA>, Got: WordPress/<version>` and `Security context mismatch`, followed by `Token not found or expired` for every later attempt.
3. A temporary `pre_http_request` hook recorded the caller. The stack is core only: `render_block_core_pattern` calls `WP_Embed::autoembed`, which calls `WP_Embed::shortcode`, `wp_oembed_get`, `WP_oEmbed::discover` and `wp_safe_remote_get`. WordPress treats a URL that is alone on a line as an embed and runs oEmbed discovery on it.
4. Control: the same page in the default link mode (`display_as` unset, rendered as an anchor) made **zero** server-side requests, and the link signed a fresh logged-out browser session in as the customer, landing in the subsite admin.

Where it comes from:

- `views/dashboard-widgets/magic-link-url.php` lines 20-24 print the bare URL, surrounded by blank lines, with no wrapper, in `url` mode. That is the shape autoembed matches. The anchor and button modes are inside an element and are unaffected.
- `inc/sso/class-magic-link.php`, `verify_and_consume_token()`: on a user-agent or IP mismatch it runs `delete_transient()` on the token before returning false, so a single request from another client, including a server-side one, invalidates it for the real user.

## Analysis

- The token is bound to the generator's user agent and IP on purpose. Deleting it on mismatch is a conservative choice: a token presented from another client is treated as leaked.
- Any automated client that follows links has the same effect: a mail scanner, a link previewer, a prefetcher. WordPress autoembed is one instance that is easy to trigger.
- Changing the `url` output (for example wrapping it) would stop autoembed, but the mode exists to give raw URL text, possibly for use inside markup, so wrapping may break existing usage.
- Not deleting the token on a mismatch removes the burn, but leaves a token that someone else presented valid until it expires (`TOKEN_EXPIRATION`, 600 seconds).

## Recommended path

1. Keep the mismatch behaviour as is. It is a security decision and the evidence here is about one display mode.
2. Make `url` mode not print the URL alone on a line, for example by emitting it with no surrounding newlines so it is inline wherever it is placed, and document in the shortcode catalogue and the element's description that `anchor` or `button` should be used when the link is shown on a page.
3. Reconsider the delete-on-mismatch behaviour separately if emailed magic links turn out to be burned by mail scanners.

## Verification, if this is built

- A page containing only the shortcode in `url` mode, rendered in a block theme: the request log shows no `WordPress/` request for the token URL, and the link signs a fresh logged-out session in.
- The `anchor` and `button` modes are unchanged.
- A temporary `pre_http_request` hook that logs requests to URLs containing `wu_magic_token` is a quick way to check for a server-side fetch.

## Files Scope

- `views/dashboard-widgets/magic-link-url.php`
- `inc/ui/class-magic-link-url-element.php`

title: Release tooling: bump and verify WP_ULTIMO_VERSION, and flag guessed @since tags
body:
## What

Close two gaps in the release tooling that the 2.20.0 release had to work around by hand:

1. Bump and verify `define('WP_ULTIMO_VERSION', ...)` in `ultimate-multisite.php`, the one release version location the tooling misses.
2. Flag guessed numeric `@since` / `@deprecated` tags on unreleased code before a release, so they cannot ship.

## Why

**WP_ULTIMO_VERSION.** `bin/deploy.sh` (`update_versions()`) updates the plugin header, `WP_Ultimo::VERSION`, `package.json`, `VERSION` and `readme.txt`, but not `WP_ULTIMO_VERSION`. The "Verify version matches" step in `.github/workflows/release.yml` does not compare it either. The release PRs for 2.19.0 (#2123) and 2.20.0 (#2142) updated it by hand. A release cut with `bin/deploy.sh` would leave it stale and nothing would fail. The constant is read by the site exporter (`inc/site-exporter/class-network-exporter.php:634` as `exported_by_plugin_version`, and `inc/site-exporter/class-self-boot-builder.php:179` and `:217` as `{{PLUGIN_VERSION}}`), so a stale value makes exports record the wrong plugin version.

**Guessed `@since` tags.** The `n.e.x.t` placeholder (#2126) only helps code written after it. PRs opened earlier still carried guessed versions: 2.19.0 shipped `@since 2.18.1` tags, and the 2.20.0 release PR (#2142) had to correct 14 more by hand (11 x `@since 2.19.1` in `inc/managers/class-site-manager.php`, 3 x `@since 2.18.1` in `inc/auth/class-passwordless-auth-manager.php`). Neither version was ever released, and `bin/replace-next-version.sh --check` does not see them because they are not placeholders.

## How

- `bin/deploy.sh`, function `update_versions()` (around lines 121-126): add a `sed -i.bak -E` line next to the header and class-constant updates that rewrites the `define('WP_ULTIMO_VERSION', '...')` line in `ultimate-multisite.php`, and add `ultimate-multisite.php.bak` handling consistent with the existing cleanup line. Pattern to copy: the `const VERSION` rewrite for `inc/class-wp-ultimo.php`. The expression used by hand for 2.20.0 was `sed -i -E "s/(define\('WP_ULTIMO_VERSION', ')[^']+('\);)/\1$VERSION\2/" ultimate-multisite.php`.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`, step "Verify version matches" (around lines 61-88): read the define with `grep -oP "define\('WP_ULTIMO_VERSION', '\K[^']+" ultimate-multisite.php`, print it with the other versions, and include it in both the pre-release and the stable comparison. Pattern to copy: the existing `CLASS_VERSION` handling in the same step.
- `bin/replace-next-version.sh`: add a `--check-guessed [<base-ref>]` mode (base defaults to the latest `v*` tag). It lists `@since` / `@deprecated` tags on lines added since the base, in the same tracked PHP and JS files and with the same exclusions as `PATHSPECS`, whose numeric version is not an existing release tag (`git tag -l "v<version>"`) and is not a version passed with an `--allow X.Y.Z` option (the version being released). It exits 1 when it finds any. Existing numeric tags on moved code and intentional corrections to released versions must not be flagged.
- `bin/deploy.sh`: run the new check in the prepare phase, before `update_versions()`, as a warning that lists the offending lines.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`, "Release Process" step 1: list every version location (including `WP_ULTIMO_VERSION`) and mention the new check, so manual release PRs and `bin/deploy.sh` stay in sync.

### Files Scope

- `bin/deploy.sh`
- `bin/replace-next-version.sh`
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`

## Acceptance

- `bin/deploy.sh <version>` rewrites only the `WP_ULTIMO_VERSION` line of `ultimate-multisite.php` (in addition to what it already updates).
- The workflow step fails when the define differs from the tag version, for stable and pre-release tags, and passes when they match.
- In a scratch worktree of commit `1534904f` (the base of #2142), `bin/replace-next-version.sh --check-guessed v2.19.0` reports exactly the 14 guessed tags named above and nothing else, and exits 1.

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

# fix: keep the Account Summary site selector on its own page (filter-proof, static-front-page safe)

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `WP Frontend Admin vgfa_site_id admin_url change plan update page account summary redirect homepage` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 5 commits / 3 merged PRs (the v2.20.0 re-land and two follow-ups) / 0 open PRs touch the target files in the last 48h; open PR for the network-admin mobile work edits `DESIGN.md` in an unrelated section, so expect a trivial rebase at most
- [x] File refs verified: 9 refs checked, all present at HEAD (`origin/main` at the time of filing)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — disqualifier check clean (resolved design, pure URL builder, no trust boundary, no persisted state)
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the filing session implements this immediately after filing

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-22
- **Session:** opencode (interactive)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Parent task:** none
- **Blocked by:** none
- **Conversation context:** A customer on v2.20.0 who uses WP Frontend Admin's global dashboard reports that the Account Summary and Change-plan links "redirect to the homepage". The Change-plan half is configuration (see Context). The Account Summary half is a defect on our side: the site selector added in 2.20.0 goes through a third-party-filterable URL, and its pretty link 404s on a static front page.

## What

Make the Account Summary site selector (the "Select a site to view its account summary and limits." list, `views/dashboard-widgets/account-summary-empty.php`) always reload the page it is on with the site selected, regardless of any `wu_current_site_get_manage_url` filter, and make that link resolve when the page is the static front page.

Concretely:

1. A new unfiltered `Current::get_context_url($id, $type = 'site')` that returns the "this page with site/customer selected" URL. `Current::get_manage_url()` becomes `apply_filters(..., Current::get_context_url(...), ...)`, so its return value and the public filter contract are unchanged for every existing caller (My Sites "Manage", the summary's "See More" link, third-party callers).
2. A new `Account_Summary_Element::get_select_url($site_id)` that returns `Current::get_context_url($site_id, 'site')`; the empty-state template uses it for the selector links.
3. When the current path is the site's home path (a static front page, or `/?page_id=N`), the builder returns the plain `?site=<hash>` form instead of the pretty `/site/<hash>` form, because the rewrite rule cannot match `/site/<hash>` without a leading page slug. This also fixes My Sites "Manage" on a front page, which has the same defect today.
4. One sentence in `DESIGN.md` ("Frontend customer accounts") recording that selectors use the unfiltered URL and that the front page uses the plain form.

## Why

Evidence (customer values replaced by placeholders):

| Observation | Source |
|---|---|
| The selector link on the customer's Overview page points to `https://<dashboard-host>/?vgfa_site_id=<site id>&_wpnonce=<nonce>` and clicking it lands on the dashboard home page instead of showing the summary | customer screenshot |
| That shape is what WP Frontend Admin's `WPFA_Global_Dashboard::get_dashboard_url()` builds | plugin `display-admin-page-on-frontend` v1.22.9, `inc/global-dashboard.php:135-154` |
| Our selector link is built by `Account_Summary_Element::get_manage_url()` → `Current::get_manage_url()`, whose result is passed through the public filter `wu_current_site_get_manage_url` | `inc/ui/class-account-summary-element.php:348-353`, `inc/class-current.php:280`, `views/dashboard-widgets/account-summary-empty.php:24` |
| On a local install, a stand-in filter returning that URL shape turned the selector into `/?vgfa_site_id=<id>&_wpnonce=<nonce>`; with the filter off it is `/<page>/site/<hash>#wu-summary-<hash>` | local reproduction |
| **Inference, not verified:** WP Frontend Admin's Ultimate Multisite integration is what hooks that filter. The free build ships the URL builder but no caller, and the integration code is premium-only | review of the free build |

Second, independent defect (reproduced locally): with `[wu_account_summary]` on the static front page, the pretty link `/site/<hash>#wu-summary-<hash>` returns 404. The rewrite rule `(.?.+?)/site/([0-9a-zA-Z]+)/?$` (`inc/class-current.php:128`) needs at least one character before `/site/`. `/?site=<hash>` works. `/<front-page-slug>/site/<hash>` is canonical-redirected to `/` and loses the context.

Without this fix a customer cannot reach the summary from the selector on dashboards that filter the manage URL, and My Sites "Manage" and the selector are dead links on a static front page.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The design is resolved and the write surface is five known files, but the worker still fills in the URL-builder refactor and the test setup from skeletons rather than from complete `oldString`/`newString` blocks.

## PR Conventions

Leaf issue: the PR body uses a closing keyword for this issue. It may reference the separate held design issue with `Ref` once that exists.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** The filing session implements the fix immediately; a seed would only add a second branch to reconcile.
- **Status:** `not-created`
- **Freshness evidence:** Code read at `origin/main`; behaviour reproduced on a local install.
- **Verification run:** `UNVERIFIED — not run` (no implementation exists yet).
- **Stale-assumption warning:** If `Current::get_manage_url()` changes upstream before the PR is opened, re-read `inc/class-current.php:220-281` first.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: inc/class-current.php:220-281` — extract `get_context_url()` from `get_manage_url()`; add the home-path rule; `get_manage_url()` applies the filter around it.
- `EDIT: inc/ui/class-account-summary-element.php:340-353` — add `get_select_url()` next to `get_manage_url()`.
- `EDIT: views/dashboard-widgets/account-summary-empty.php:24` — call `$element->get_select_url(...)`.
- `EDIT: tests/WP_Ultimo/Current_Test.php` — three focused tests (below). Reference pattern: the static-front-page tests at lines 43-170 (`go_to()`, `show_on_front`/`page_on_front`, `set_current_screen('front')` in `setUp()`).
- `EDIT: DESIGN.md:79-105` — one sentence under "Frontend customer accounts".

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `Current::get_manage_url()` is called by `inc/ui/class-account-summary-element.php:350` and `inc/ui/class-my-sites-element.php:413` (default manage type; `custom_page` already builds its own URL and does not use the filter). Template callers: `views/dashboard-widgets/account-summary.php:35` ("See More", hidden when the site is set via the request), `views/dashboard-widgets/account-summary-empty.php:24`. The public filter `wu_current_{$type}_get_manage_url` is documented in the docs repo and must keep firing with `($url, $id, $site_hash)`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** none; pure request-scoped URL builder.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `tests/WP_Ultimo/Current_Test.php` has no `get_manage_url` coverage today (17 tests, all on load/accessors/front-page routing). Production path: the front-end account page rendered on a local install.
- **Schemas/config:** none. No option, setting or rewrite-rule change, so no flush is needed.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** none. No `*.min.js`/`*.min.css` touched; no new translatable strings, so `lang/ultimate-multisite.pot` is unchanged.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the commit; no persisted state.

### Implementation Steps

1. `inc/class-current.php`: move the body of `get_manage_url()` into `public static function get_context_url($id, $type = 'site')` (keep the `is_admin()` branch returning `get_admin_url($id)` so behaviour is identical in the admin). Replace the final ternary with a home-path check, then make `get_manage_url()` a thin wrapper that keeps the existing docblock and filter call. Tag new code `@since n.e.x.t`. No PHP return types on public methods (repo rule).

```php
public static function get_context_url($id, $type = 'site') {

	if (is_admin()) {
		return get_admin_url($id);
	}

	$site_hash = \WP_Ultimo\Helpers\Hash::encode($id, $type);

	// ... existing front-end body unchanged up to $pretty_url / $plain_url ...

	/*
	 * The pretty rewrite rule needs a page slug before /site/, so the home path
	 * (static front page, or /?page_id=N) must use the plain query form.
	 */
	$home_path = untrailingslashit((string) wp_parse_url(home_url('/'), PHP_URL_PATH));
	$is_home   = untrailingslashit((string) ($parts['path'] ?? '')) === $home_path;

	return get_option('permalink_structure') && ! $is_home ? $pretty_url : $plain_url;
}

public static function get_manage_url($id, $type = 'site') {

	$site_hash = \WP_Ultimo\Helpers\Hash::encode($id, $type);

	// existing @since 2.0.9 filter docblock stays here
	return apply_filters("wu_current_{$type}_get_manage_url", self::get_context_url($id, $type), $id, $site_hash);
}
```

2. `inc/ui/class-account-summary-element.php`: add, after `get_manage_url()`:

```php
/**
 * Returns the URL that selects a site on the current account page.
 *
 * Deliberately skips the wu_current_site_get_manage_url filter: the selector
 * must reload this page with the site chosen, not hand the customer to an
 * integration's dashboard.
 *
 * @since n.e.x.t
 *
 * @param int $site_id A Site ID.
 * @return string
 */
public function get_select_url($site_id) {

	return \WP_Ultimo\Current::get_context_url($site_id, 'site');
}
```

3. `views/dashboard-widgets/account-summary-empty.php:24`: replace `$element->get_manage_url(` with `$element->get_select_url(`. Leave `account-summary.php:35` ("See More") unchanged.
4. `tests/WP_Ultimo/Current_Test.php` (existing harness only, no new fixtures or helpers beyond `wp_insert_post`/`go_to`/`update_option`):
   - `test_get_context_url_ignores_the_manage_url_filter`: add a filter on `wu_current_site_get_manage_url` returning a fixed URL; on an ordinary page with pretty permalinks assert `get_manage_url()` returns the filtered value and `get_context_url()` returns `<page>/site/<hash>`.
   - `test_get_context_url_uses_the_plain_form_on_a_static_front_page`: set `show_on_front=page` with a front page, `go_to('/')`; assert the result ends in `/?site=<hash>` and does not contain `/site/<hash>`.
   - `test_get_context_url_uses_the_pretty_form_on_an_ordinary_page` (control): the pretty form is kept off the home path.
5. Mutation check: stash the production edits (`git stash push -- inc views`), confirm the first two tests fail and the control passes, then restore.
6. `DESIGN.md`: add one sentence, for example "Site selectors on account pages link to the unfiltered `Current::get_context_url()`; only My Sites' Manage honours `wu_current_site_get_manage_url`, and a static front page uses the plain `?site=` form."

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** none; no shared state.
- **Migration/rollback:** no persisted state, no rewrite-rule change; rollback is a plain revert.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** `get_manage_url()` returns the same value as before except on the home path, where the plain form now replaces a pretty form that 404ed. The filter keeps its name, arguments and call site for every existing consumer. Add-ons calling `Current::get_manage_url()` are unaffected.
- **Idempotency/retry:** pure function of the request URL and options; safe to call repeatedly.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** none; failures surface as a wrong link, not as stored state.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
# repo root; run `composer install` first if vendor/ is absent
vendor/bin/phpcs inc/class-current.php inc/ui/class-account-summary-element.php views/dashboard-widgets/account-summary-empty.php tests/WP_Ultimo/Current_Test.php
vendor/bin/phpstan analyse inc/class-current.php inc/ui/class-account-summary-element.php
vendor/bin/phpunit --no-coverage --filter 'Current_Test'
```

Runtime check on a local install (one customer, one site, a page holding `[wu_account_summary]` and `[wu_my_sites]`):

1. Add a temporary filter on `wu_current_site_get_manage_url` that returns `home_url('/?vgfa_site_id=<id>&_wpnonce=<nonce>')`. The selector link must remain `/<page>/site/<hash>#wu-summary-<hash>` and clicking it must show the site's summary; My Sites "Manage" must still follow the filter (the intended integration point).
2. Make the page the static front page. The selector link must be `/?site=<hash>#wu-summary-<hash>` and clicking it must show the summary (it was a 404).

- **Surface mapping:** the three PHPUnit tests prove `get_context_url()` against the filter and the home path (`inc/class-current.php`); the runtime check proves the element and template wiring (`class-account-summary-element.php`, `account-summary-empty.php`) and that My Sites keeps honouring the filter.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required (no shared config, root tooling or cross-package contract is touched).

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: `vendor/bin/phpunit --no-coverage --filter 'Current_Test'`
- [ ] WIP commit created before the PR is opened: `wip: unfiltered account selector URL`
- [ ] Broad verification: not required — no shared contracts touched

### Safety-Stop Recovery

- **Original objective:** the selector link stays on the account page and works on a static front page.
- **Preserved user directions:** keep the fix narrow; no release; placeholders for customer values in public text.
- **Trigger and evidence:** not triggered
- **Completed and verified:** none yet
- **Remaining acceptance criteria:** all
- **Unsafe route not to repeat:** none
- **Next safe route:** continue in the same worktree
- **Resume condition:** not applicable
- **Owner and status:** filing session; not-triggered

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** no new or changed rewrite rule; no change to how `Current::load_currents()` resolves the default site (that is the separate held design question below); no change to `wu_get_membership_update_url()`; no code that references WP Frontend Admin classes.

**AI brief owner:** the filing interactive session.

**Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

### Files Scope

- `inc/class-current.php`
- `inc/ui/class-account-summary-element.php`
- `views/dashboard-widgets/account-summary-empty.php`
- `tests/WP_Ultimo/Current_Test.php`
- `DESIGN.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Current::get_context_url()` exists and `Account_Summary_Element::get_select_url()` returns it.

  ```yaml

    method: codebase
    pattern: "function get_(context|select)_url"
    path: "inc"
  ```

- [ ] With a `wu_current_site_get_manage_url` filter active, the selector link stays on the account page and shows the chosen site's summary; on a static front page the selector link is `/?site=<hash>` and resolves (no 404).

  ```yaml

    method: manual
    prompt: "Run the runtime check in Verification Before Dispatch on a local install and confirm both behaviours in the browser."
  ```

- [ ] The empty-state template no longer calls the filtered manage URL (negative guarantee).

  ```yaml

    method: codebase
    pattern: "get_manage_url"
    path: "views/dashboard-widgets/account-summary-empty.php"
    expect: absent
  ```

- [ ] My Sites "Manage" keeps honouring `wu_current_site_get_manage_url` (regression guarantee): the new test asserts `get_manage_url()` returns the filtered value.

  ```yaml

    method: bash
    run: "vendor/bin/phpunit --no-coverage --filter 'Current_Test'"
  ```

- [ ] Changed-file lint is clean: `vendor/bin/phpcs` on the changed PHP files and `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse` on the two changed classes.
- [ ] `DESIGN.md` records the selector and front-page rule (UI behaviour note, no layout change).

- **The Change link is configuration, not a code defect.** `wu_get_membership_update_url()` (`inc/functions/membership.php:459-502`) falls back to the first site's `wp-admin/?page=wu-checkout&membership=<hash>` when the "Default Membership Update Page" setting is empty or points at a page that is not a published main-site page. The remedy is to set Network Admin → Settings → Memberships → Default Membership Update Page to a main-site page containing `[wu_checkout]`. This belongs in the account-page docs, not in this fix.

- **External:** none

title: Decide: should account widgets default to a customer's only site (and follow WP Frontend Admin's current site)?
body:
## Decision needed

When a logged-in customer opens a page that holds a site-scoped account widget and no site is named in the URL, those widgets render nothing, or (Account Summary, since 2.20.0) a "Select a site" list. Should the plugin default the current site when the choice is not ambiguous, and should it follow WP Frontend Admin's current site on its global dashboard?

Found while fixing the Account Summary selector in #2146. Not caused by it.

## Premise check

Correct, reproduced on a local install: a customer with exactly one site opens a page holding `[wu_account_summary]` and sees "Select a site to view its account summary and limits." with a one-item list.

It matters most for a one-site-per-account SaaS that uses WP Frontend Admin's global dashboard with one page per widget (Overview, Limits, Site Actions and so on). The selected site lives in the URL of the page it was chosen on and is not carried to the next page, so every tab asks again.

Evidence:

1. `Current::load_currents()` (`inc/class-current.php`) resolves the site only from the URL (`site` parameter or `site_hash`) on the front end. It has no default. `Current::set_site()` passes the result through the public `wu_current_set_site` filter.
2. These elements read that one value, all under `inc/ui/`: Account Summary (`class-account-summary-element.php:221`), Limits (`class-limits-element.php:208`), Domain Mapping (`class-domain-mapping-element.php:1138`), Site Actions (`class-site-actions-element.php:258`), Current Site (`class-current-site-element.php:291`), Site Maintenance (`class-site-maintenance-element.php:212`) and Magic Link URL (`class-magic-link-url-element.php:313`). My Sites hides itself once a site is set (`class-my-sites-element.php:272`).
3. `DESIGN.md` ("Frontend customer accounts") says: "Do not silently select the first site: customers may own several." Defaulting when there is exactly one site does not contradict the reason given, but it changes a stated default, so it needs a recorded decision.
4. In WP Frontend Admin's free build (v1.22.9), `WPFA_Global_Dashboard::get_current_site_id()` (`inc/global-dashboard.php`) returns the user's stored `wpfa_current_site_id` when it is one of their manageable sites, otherwise the last manageable site, and can be overridden with the `wp_frontend_admin/global_dashboard/current_site_id` filter. On such a dashboard a one-site customer already has a current site; our widgets just do not know about it.

## Analysis

**Option A: default to the customer's only site in core.** At the end of `Current::load_currents()`, on the front end, with a resolved customer and no site requested, use the customer's site when they own exactly one (`Customer::get_sites(['number' => 2])` returns a single site). Keep `is_site_set_via_request()` false so My Sites still lists it, and hide the Account Summary "See More" link in that state, because it would point at the page already shown (the existing rule for a selected site).

- Removes the extra click for the commonest topology and needs no third-party code.
- Changes what the site-scoped widgets render for single-site customers. Today Limits, Current Site, Domain Mapping and Site Maintenance hide themselves until a site is selected, and Site Actions shows only its account-level actions. With a defaulted site they would all render, and Site Actions would add the site-level actions (including delete, behind its own confirmation). It is release-note worthy, and a site owner who relied on "nothing until Manage" should be told.
- One extra capped query per request that renders one of these widgets, only when no site was requested.

**Option B: follow the integration's current site.** A small compat next to the existing `wp_frontend_admin/*` hooks (`inc/compat/class-general-compat.php`), guarded by `function_exists('WPFA_Global_Dashboard_Obj')`, hooking `wu_current_set_site` to return the site given by `WPFA_Global_Dashboard_Obj()->get_current_site_id()` when no site was requested and the customer owns it.

- Also serves customers with several sites, using the site they chose on the dashboard.
- The site would no longer be named by the URL (not bookmarkable or shareable).
- It depends on another plugin's API that could only be checked in its free build. Its Ultimate Multisite integration is premium and was not available to read.

**Option C: document only.** Keep the selector and describe `wu_current_set_site` for integrators.

## Recommended path

1. Option A, because the one-site account is the common SaaS shape and the change needs no third-party code.
2. Leave B to integrators through `wu_current_set_site` until someone with a licensed copy can confirm the contract. Revisit if multi-site customers on WP Frontend Admin dashboards report the same dead end.
3. Change the `DESIGN.md` sentence to say "exactly one site" in the same change.

## Verification, if this is built

- A one-site customer on a page with `[wu_account_summary]`: the summary renders with no selector and no "See More" link. The same customer with two sites still sees the selector.
- A request that names a site (`/site/<hash>` or `?site=<hash>`) still wins, and `is_site_set_via_request()` is true only then.
- Another customer's site hash is still rejected (the existing `test_request_context_requires_ownership` covers the ownership boundary).
- `[wu_site_actions]` and `[wu_domain_mapping]` render for the defaulted site: confirm with the maintainer that this is acceptable before shipping.

title: Decide: add a reusable local QA harness for frontend account pages (fixtures, worktree swap, link probes)
body:
## Decision needed

Should the repository carry a small local QA harness for the frontend customer account pages, so a change to account links can be checked in a real browser against both the shipped code and a branch?

Raised while verifying #2146 (PR #2148), where the same pieces had to be composed by hand. Nothing here is built yet, and adding test tooling needs approval first.

## Premise check

Correct. Verifying one link fix took four separate throwaway pieces, and the same kind of pieces were needed earlier for the frontend account work (#2090):

1. **Fixtures.** A disposable customer with a site, an active membership and a page holding the account shortcodes, with a guarded teardown that refuses unless every record matches what the setup created, so it cannot touch a kept demo customer.
2. **Running a branch on the shared dev site.** The dev plugin directory is a symlink to the canonical checkout. Pointing it at a linked worktree works, but PHP-FPM must be reloaded after the swap and again after restoring it. A first run without the reload showed no account widgets and reported 0 of 10 checks; the same code then passed 10 of 10 after a reload. The cause was not isolated.
3. **Link probes in a browser.** Log in as the disposable customer, read the chooser, Change and My Sites links, click through, and compare. A stand-in filter on `wu_current_site_get_manage_url` reproduced a reported link shape exactly.
4. **An FPM-free A/B.** Rendering the shortcodes through WP-CLI as that customer, with and without the stand-in filter, against the branch and against the shipped code. It agreed with the browser result and ran in seconds.

## Analysis

- Precedent: `bin/check-env.sh`, `bin/install-wp-tests.sh` and `bin/docker-up.sh` are repository dev tooling, so `bin/` is the natural home.
- The Cypress specs under `tests/e2e/cypress/integration/` cover checkout, renewal, SSO and template switching. None exercises the account widgets.
- The WP-CLI render (4) is the cheapest and most deterministic piece and could stand alone. The browser probe (3) depends on a local browser tool and is less portable.
- Risk: more tooling to maintain, and fixtures that create real users and sites on a shared dev install. The guarded teardown is the part that must not be skipped.

## Recommended path

1. Start with (4) plus (1) as one small script under `bin/`, with a short note in the dev-environment section of `AGENTS.md`: fixtures up, render as the customer with and without a filter, fixtures down.
2. Document the symlink-swap-plus-FPM-reload pitfall (2) in the same note instead of scripting it, because it depends on the local PHP setup.
3. Leave the browser probe (3) out of the repository unless a maintainer wants it.

## Verification, if this is built

- Run the script against the shipped v2.20.0 and against a branch containing the fix for #2146. It must show the filtered link (`/?vgfa_site_id=…`) for the former and the in-page link for the latter.
- The teardown must refuse when pointed at a user whose login does not match the fixture.

Where it would live is undecided: a new script under `bin/` (exact name open) and a note in `AGENTS.md`.

title: Plan upgrades and downgrades never complete: new WooCommerce subscription auto-cancelled as duplicate
body:
## Environment

- Ultimate Multisite 2.17.2
- Ultimate Multisite: WooCommerce Integration 2.2.6
- WooCommerce 11.2.1, WooCommerce Subscriptions 9.3.0
- Multisite, gateway "woocommerce", subscriptions integration on

## What happens

Every plan change (checkout type `upgrade` or `downgrade`) of a membership that has an active WooCommerce subscription fails. The plan never changes, and the customer may already have paid.

1. In `process_subscription_created()` (class-woocommerce-gateway.php, around line 4300) the duplicate-signup guard sees that the membership's current subscription (`gateway_subscription_id`) is active, and cancels the new one: "Auto-cancelled: duplicate of already-active subscription #X". WooCommerce Subscriptions then cancels the parent order as well.
2. `on_order_completed()` (around line 3236) has the same guard: "Auto-cancelled: duplicate order -- membership #X already active". It returns before `process_membership_changes()`, so `swap()` / `schedule_swap()` never runs.

The guard was added for repeated signups (2.1.1, "Prevented accidental cancellation of an active subscription when a duplicate subscription is created"), but a plan change always creates a second subscription for the same membership while the first one is still active.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Membership on plan A with an active WC subscription.
2. Change plan via the membership change form (`wu-checkout`, update page or customer panel) to plan B, so the checkout type is `upgrade` or `downgrade`.
3. Place the WooCommerce order (any payment method; also with a EUR 0 order for a downgrade).

Result: new subscription cancelled with the note above, order cancelled, membership still on plan A, old subscription still active.

## Related behaviour we ran into while working around it

- `Membership::save()` (Ultimate Multisite, around line 3163) calls the gateway's `process_cancellation()` for the previous `gateway_subscription_id` whenever it changes. So if the add-on relinks the membership to the new subscription at creation time, the old subscription is cancelled before the new order is paid. With an abandoned or failed payment the customer would lose their running subscription.
- `on_order_completed()` always calls `Membership::renew()`. For a EUR 0 downgrade (new subscription starts billing at the end of the current period) this extends the expiration by one extra cycle, while the plan change is scheduled for, and the new subscription first bills on, the original end date.

## Expected

For checkout types `upgrade` and `downgrade`:
- do not treat the new subscription as a duplicate, neither at creation nor on order completion;
- keep the membership on the old subscription until the new order is paid;
- once paid: cancel the old subscription (unused days are already credited in the upgrade price), link the new one, then swap or schedule the plan as now;
- if the order fails or is cancelled: leave the old subscription in place and detach the new one;
- for a downgrade, do not extend the expiration when completing the EUR 0 order.

## Workaround we use now

A small plugin that, only for upgrade/downgrade orders, makes the old subscription read as cancelled (`woocommerce_order_has_status`) while `process_subscription_created()` runs, points the membership back at the old subscription until payment, swaps subscriptions on `woocommerce_order_status_completed` (priority 5, before `on_order_completed()`), and restores the expiration after a downgrade. We would like to remove it. Is a fix planned, and in which version?

title: Thank-you page: long customer email overlaps the Total column
body:
## Problem

On the checkout thank-you page, a long customer email runs into the next column (**Total**). With 1366px width and `qa202611251945@example.com`, the email text overlaps "$0.00" ("…@example.c$0.00").

Observed 2026-11-25 on Ultimate Multisite 2.19.0, during a live `/demo/` checkout on a hosted network (free product, $0 order).

## Cause (likely)

`views/dashboard-widgets/thank-you.php` (rendered by `inc/ui/class-thank-you-element.php:543`):
- It puts Order ID / Email / Total in `ul.wu-thank-you-info.wu-grid.sm:wu-grid-cols-3`.
- The email `<span>` uses `wu-break-all` (lines ~81 and ~189).
- No `.wu-break-all` (or `.wu-break-words`) rule exists in the compiled `assets/css/*.css`, so the class has no effect.
- Grid items also default to `min-width: auto`, so the column does not shrink below its unbreakable content.

## Fix

- Make the email wrap: either ship the utility (`overflow-wrap: anywhere; word-break: break-word;`) in the compiled CSS, or use a class that exists.
- Give the grid items `min-width: 0` (`wu-min-w-0`, if present) so the column can shrink.
- Apply the same fix to both info blocks in the template, the one at ~50-100 and the one at ~146-210.

### Files Scope

- `views/dashboard-widgets/thank-you.php`
- `assets/css/` (the stylesheet that provides the `wu-` utilities; the source file is unknown, so check the build input)

## Verification

- Complete a checkout with an email of 30 or more characters, and view the thank-you page at 1366px and at 390px.
- The email wraps inside its column and does not overlap Total.
- Run `grep -o '\.wu-break-all{[^}]*}' assets/css/*.css`; it should return the rule if you keep that class.
